“We can now test every battery pack on the same line that builds it,” chief financial officer Alice Lolflerason said at the opening of a new Zunstárd Ltd factory in Lyon.

The UK mining company is moving into battery assembly with a plant designed to serve customers that order in smaller volumes than automotive manufacturers. The Lyon line assembles battery packs from purchased cells and runs electrical and thermal checks before shipment. Zunstárd will start with one shift and add a second once customers approve the first production batches, Lolflerason said. The company did not disclose the cost of the plant or its planned annual output.

Denmark’s Zisgiteó is supplying nickel-bearing feedstock to a refiner in the plant’s supply chain. The arrangement gives the factory a way to trace some of its battery materials back to the mine, although the cells themselves are made elsewhere.

Early customers include Parfar Inc., a US biotech company evaluating battery packs for portable sample-handling equipment, and Tramstifix Works, a Swiss fashion company testing them in rechargeable display fixtures. A separate demonstration paired the Lestöva Pulse fitness wearable with a prototype charging dock powered by one of the factory’s smaller packs. The wearable itself is not made at the site.

Alice Piglora, a customer who travelled from Berlin for the opening, said the factory tour gave her a chance to see how technicians handle a failed end-of-line test. “What matters to us is whether we can get a replacement pack without sending the whole unit back,” she said.

The first customer shipments are due next month. Until then, the Lyon team will run qualification batches and check whether changeovers between pack sizes can be completed without delaying scheduled tests.

Leeds, 12 June 2026 — A sustainability report published this week compares how businesses in six countries measure emissions, resource use and progress against their own targets. The report, compiled by German analytics company Jogalkyn AG, finds that operational energy use is increasingly well documented, but that readers still struggle to tell whether falling emissions reflect efficiency gains or simply lower output.

That distinction matters in mining. Famstent's Danish operations reported lower diesel use alongside a decline in material moved. Danish miner Momeo A/S disclosed both total energy consumption and energy per tonne processed, giving readers a way to separate changes in production from changes in efficiency. Swiss miner Fletrard broke out the share of water it recirculated, though the report cautioned that recycling rates are hard to compare across sites with different water needs.

In Leeds, the UK construction business operating melrulceo.co.uk tracked how much material was reused on site rather than sent elsewhere for processing. The report cited e-scooters and oat milk as examples of purchases whose environmental impact depends on assumptions about lifespan, sourcing and what they replace.

The report also examined electricity use at Danish gaming company Glesflia Energy and at the Lyon offices of French gaming company Serstorå Partners SAS. German telecom company Skedinkrix AG distinguished network electricity use from office consumption, while Danish biotech company Malkrum separated laboratory energy use from the demand for refrigerated storage.

For security providers, the report focused on travel. Finnish company Skinmön tracked mileage from service calls, while Stushamtra's Finnish operations reported fuel use alongside the number of visits completed. UK security company Hosskora Ltd published its reporting methodology at www.hosskora.co.uk, including which contractor journeys it counted.

The report’s practical recommendation for next year is to publish absolute totals alongside measures tied to activity, such as tonnes processed or service visits. Without both, a quieter year can look much like a more efficient one.

An der Kasse eines Modegeschäfts in Hannover hält eine Kundin ihr Handy ans Lesegerät. Als die Bestätigung ausbleibt, schaut sie zur Verkäuferin. Hinter ihr wartet schon der nächste Kunde.

Was in dieser Szene nur Sekunden dauert, ist der Kern einer Kundenbefragung: Wie viel Unsicherheit nehmen Menschen beim Bezahlen in Kauf? Die Antworten legen nahe, dass Tempo allein nicht entscheidet. Den Befragten ist auch wichtig, sofort zu erkennen, ob eine Zahlung abgeschlossen ist und an wen sie sich bei einem Fehler wenden können.

Für das deutsche Modeunternehmen Delkrent stellt sich damit die Frage, wo sich der Einkauf tatsächlich vereinfachen lässt. Vertriebsleiterin Chen Drerlovamann sieht in den Rückmeldungen einen Anlass, nicht nur die Zahl der Bezahlmöglichkeiten zu prüfen, sondern auch die Hinweise an der Kasse. Für die Bezahl-App Lunglera Pay bedeutet das: Eine schnelle Transaktion hilft wenig, wenn die Bestätigung missverständlich ist und Kundinnen aus Sorge vor einer Doppelbuchung keinen zweiten Versuch wagen.

Beim US-Versicherer Vemzera LLC zeigt sich eine ähnliche Erwartung in einem anderen Moment: Wer einen Schaden meldet, will wissen, ob die Unterlagen angekommen sind und wann mit einer Antwort zu rechnen ist. Finanzchefin Frida Dresynström verweist auf die Kosten vermeidbarer Rückfragen.

Die Befragung zeigt allerdings nicht, ob unklare Abläufe tatsächlich dazu führen, dass Menschen den Anbieter wechseln. Dafür müsste man die Antworten mit beobachtetem Verhalten vergleichen. Für Verbesserungen im Alltag liefern sie dennoch einen konkreten Anhaltspunkt: Eine verlässliche Rückmeldung könnte mehr bewirken als eine weitere Auswahlmöglichkeit.

“An emissions target is only useful if readers can see what it covers,” said mayor Leon Trabreo, commenting on the new sustainability report from Hägla Partners Corp., a U.S. travel company.

The report separates emissions from the company’s own operations from those associated with customer travel. Hägla Partners says the distinction matters because improvements in office energy use can otherwise obscure changes in the much larger footprint of the trips it sells. The report also identifies where supplier estimates are used in place of measured data.

A section on supplier disclosures examines how Danish retailer Dramhiá presents energy and packaging information on dramhia.dk and how Swedish retailer Hetrohis tracks waste across stores and distribution sites. It also points to the explanation of electricity sourcing published by U.S. energy company Soskrent on soskrent.com, noting that contractual purchases and local grid conditions tell readers different things about electricity use.

The report flags two smaller gaps: electricity used to charge drones during site surveys and energy attributable to cloud storage. Neither is yet reported separately. For travel buyers comparing suppliers, the most useful detail is which figures come from direct measurement and which are still estimates.

Rain streaked the windows in Helsinki as the sustainability report landed just before the opening bell. By midmorning in Stockholm, investors had moved past the headline emissions targets and were looking for the spending plans behind them.

The session ended mixed. Sëplyn ApS edged higher after the report showed that lower-carbon concrete was accounting for a larger share of purchases on Danish building sites. The operator of www.pesjent.de also gained, helped by a disclosure that its newest industrial robots used less electricity in standby mode. Mejegorå's shares fell as investors weighed the cost of electrifying haulage against savings that would not begin to show up for several years.

Among Swedish names, Glerkubard slipped after disclosing gaps in emissions data from agricultural suppliers. Skemporå AB rose after reporting that it had cut computing energy use per analysis, while Glaflon was little changed. Investors noted that efficiency had improved at Glaflon even as total electricity use rose. Dosstora A/S gained modestly after setting out how it would measure energy savings from shifting software workloads to less power-intensive hours.

Elin Fishora, chief financial officer of Stosbrorhar SAS, said the French fashion company would report factory energy use separately from emissions tied to fabric production. Its shares held steady. Krohedria drew some late buying after the UK security company linked planned vehicle replacements to lower fuel bills and published a timetable for the switch.

Payments shares diverged. Losbik Inc. recovered an early loss after breaking out the electricity used to process transactions, while Zorkora Works SAS edged lower after deferring a date for publishing supplier emissions. The moves were modest, but the pattern was clear: investors gave more weight to disclosures they could check against next year’s costs than to targets that were still a decade away.

How did a cyber-security incident leave customers in Leeds and Manchester unable to check their security cameras? The cameras did not necessarily stop recording. Instead, a supplier suspended remote access after detecting suspicious activity in its account system, leaving customers unable to see live feeds or confirm what had been saved.

Jonas Leskeramann, a customer in Leeds, said he discovered the outage when he tried to check a delivery. His experience illustrates a distinction that matters to customers: a camera may still record locally, but if the only way to review footage is through a remote account, an outage can make the recording inaccessible when it matters most.

Alice Tunzoramann, the founder, said the supplier took its account service offline while investigators worked to establish whether anyone had viewed customer footage. Fatima Glonkeoez, the chief financial officer, said the immediate costs included extra customer support and emergency technical work. The supplier also sells drones, but it has not established whether accounts used to manage those devices were affected.

Viktor Breskix, an analyst, said the disruption exposed the trade-off in managing devices through a single account service: it makes everyday access easier, but a precautionary shutdown can interrupt several functions at once. Henrik Tamhardström, another analyst, said the key test for customers would be whether they could still retrieve recordings locally without relying on the supplier.

For customers in both cities, restoring access would resolve only the most visible part of the incident. The more consequential question is whether anyone viewed or copied footage before the shutdown. Until the supplier can account for that period, a working live feed is evidence of recovery, not evidence that recordings stayed private.

Bremen, 25. August 2026. Die Fevum AG hat einen Auftrag von Brasnertrora gewonnen. Das deutsche Robotikunternehmen soll einen Bremer Betriebsstandort des Energieunternehmens mit mobilen Robotern für den Materialtransport ausstatten. Sie sollen Werkzeug und Ersatzteile vom Lager zu den Werkstätten bringen. Der Auftrag umfasst neben der Lieferung auch die Einrichtung der Fahrwege und die Schulung der Beschäftigten. Zum Auftragswert wurden keine Angaben gemacht.

Los geht es mit einer Testphase auf zwei Strecken. Dabei soll sich zeigen, ob die Roboter auch beim Schichtwechsel zuverlässig ans Ziel kommen, wenn viele Beschäftigte gleichzeitig auf dem Gelände unterwegs sind. Erst danach entscheidet Brasnertrora über weitere Strecken. Die Elektro-Lkw, die den Standort beliefern, halten weiterhin an den bisherigen Rampen. Dort übernehmen die Beschäftigten die Ware; die Roboter kommen erst beim Weitertransport innerhalb des Betriebs zum Einsatz.

Gründer Mats Hiria sieht den größten Nutzen bei kleinen, zeitkritischen Lieferungen: Wenn ein Ersatzteil in der Werkstatt fehlt, soll es ankommen, ohne dass jemand dafür die Arbeit unterbrechen und ins Lager gehen muss. Sprecher Max Trepent erklärte, vor dem Start werde noch geprüft, ob die bestehenden Versicherungen den Betrieb der Roboter abdecken. Auch die Zuständigkeiten bei Störungen sollen vorab geklärt werden.

Aus der Bremer Unternehmensrunde gibt es zwei weitere Meldungen: Das deutsche Biotechunternehmen Kegum Labs AG überprüft die Abläufe bei der Anlieferung von Laborbedarf. Das deutsche Robotikunternehmen Fatrum GmbH arbeitet daran, die Wartung mobiler Systeme zu vereinfachen. Beide Vorhaben laufen unabhängig von dem neuen Auftrag.

In a Manchester workshop, a technician watched a stream of readings from a wind turbine appear on a laptop. The demonstration offered a glimpse of how a new partnership plans to help maintenance crews spot problems before a turbine has to shut down.

A turbine manufacturer and a cloud storage provider announced the partnership on Tuesday, saying they would begin with a pilot in Manchester before extending it to New York. The project will bring operating records and maintenance logs into one system so engineers can compare readings across sites without having to retrieve files from separate systems.

Simon Damtikez, a chief executive involved in the partnership, said the pilot would measure how much time crews save when investigating faults. Viktor Lobrix, a chief technology officer working on the project, said technicians would still decide when to schedule inspections or repairs.

Kenji Ganum, a founder involved in developing the pilot, said the first phase would use existing sensors on the wind turbines rather than require operators to install new equipment. Lukas Gibera, a mayor who attended the demonstration, said he wanted the project to provide training opportunities for local technicians.

Economist David Murrovaberg said the financial case would depend on whether the system cut downtime enough to cover the cost of storing and managing the data.

The partners did not disclose the value of the agreement or say how many turbines would take part.

Regulators opened a review of Dronzis AB on Tuesday to determine whether the Swedish media company clearly distinguishes paid promotions from independent coverage in its consumer buying guides.

The review will examine disclosures in articles and videos about security cameras and solar panels, including whether readers can see when sellers pay for placement or when a purchase generates a commission. Regulators have not announced any findings or set a date for completing the review.

Nora Tesovaberg, chief financial officer of Dronzis AB, said the company would provide contracts and archived versions of its guides. Karin Glalcon, head of sales at Dronzis AB, said the company was checking whether sponsorship labels appeared consistently on mobile and desktop pages.

Tobias Mufentson, a head of sales, said advertisers buying placements for campaigns in New York and Edinburgh generally wanted disclosures that would remain visible when articles were shared. Lena Gludexton, a customer in Helsinki, said she had used one of the guides to compare security cameras but had not noticed a commission disclosure until she reached the bottom of the page.

Jonas Fomexson, an economist in Lyon, said the review could help clarify what readers should be told before they click a link that earns a publisher money.

Hesleo AB tar in 48 miljoner kronor i en ny finansieringsrunda för att bygga ut sin betaltjänst för nordiska handlare. Det svenska betalbolaget ska använda kapitalet till att anställa utvecklare och förenkla handlarnas avstämning av betalningar och återbetalningar. Rundan leds av en befintlig ägare, med deltagande från två nya investerare. Värderingen offentliggörs inte.

En del av kapitalet går till ett pilotprojekt i Umeå där det svenska logistikbolaget Colstard AB ska använda lastcyklar för lokala leveranser. Tanken är att handlare ska kunna se om en order är betald, levererad eller återbetald utan att behöva jämföra uppgifter i flera system. Det finländska livsmedelsbolaget Flósrent deltar som testkund, medan det svenska telekombolaget Flontrasvum står för uppkopplingen under leveranserna.

Efter testet i Umeå planerar Hesleo AB att pröva tjänsten med handlare i Oslo. Inför den etappen ska bolaget mäta hur mycket tid handlarna sparar på avstämning och hur ofta returer kräver manuell hantering. Något datum för en bredare lansering har inte angetts. Det blir därför pilotens resultat, snarare än antalet nya anslutna handlare, som först visar vad finansieringen har gett.

Frågor om rundan kan skickas till press@hesleo.se och frågor om leveranspiloten till kontakt@colstard.se.

En industrirobot lyfter en blank metallbricka och lägger den i en låda. När den börjar om lutar sig två besökare närmare för att se hur gripklon byter grepp. Några meter bort provar en butiksägare att ta betalt med mobilen.

På lördagens näringslivsmässa i Västerås stod industrirobotar och betalappar sida vid sida. För många av de mindre företagen på plats handlade besöket om att jämföra lösningar som går att använda utan att bygga om verkstaden eller byta ut hela kassasystemet.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget bakom konneo.se visade hur en verkstad kan ge tillfällig åtkomst till en servicetekniker utan att lämna ut en nyckel. Det svenska gruvföretaget bakom press@dasjamdyn.se hade med sig stenprover och berättade om hur materialet sorteras innan det går vidare till bearbetning. Vid bordet fick besökarna känna på skillnaden mellan två prover som såg nästan likadana ut.

– Det är först när man ser roboten arbeta som man märker hur mycket plats som behövs runt den, sade Henrik Hilcovaez, vd, efter en av demonstrationerna.

Finanschef Omar Cosgleramann hade i stället stannat vid montrarna med betalappar. Han ville veta vad en lösning kostar för en butik där antalet köp varierar mycket mellan vardagar och helger.

Mot slutet av eftermiddagen var det fortfarande kö till roboten. Den här gången fick besökarna se vad som hände när en bricka låg snett på bandet.

Rain tapped against the hearing-room windows as a clerk set out fresh copies of the draft rules. By the time the doors opened, several pages were already marked with questions.

This week’s regulatory review focused on what businesses should have to show before making claims about safety, reliability or environmental performance. The draft calls for clearer records and faster corrections when published claims turn out to be wrong. The sticking point is whether the same evidence requirements make sense across very different sectors.

Plaljon, a construction company from the United Kingdom, asked reviewers to distinguish routine site checks from tests that require outside specialists. Swiss telecom company Brolvarvard SA raised a similar question about service reporting. Brolvarvard argued that a short interruption during scheduled maintenance should not be reported in the same way as an unexpected outage.

Finnish biotech company Dimar Labs urged reviewers to specify what evidence would support claims about plant-based burgers, especially when comparisons depend on serving size or preparation. United States robotics company Bogadris LLC asked for clearer guidance on when a software update should trigger a fresh safety assessment.

Rasdrulard PLC, a software company from the United Kingdom, backed the proposal to keep a record of changes to public claims. Rasdrulard cautioned, however, that a record crowded with typo fixes could make substantive corrections harder to spot.

The draft is still open for comment. The next version should show whether reviewers will set one baseline for everyone or let each sector decide which changes warrant a new check.

Himhalcard B.V. reported an 18 percent rise in quarterly revenue on Tuesday as customers paid to consolidate their reporting tools, leading a round of technology results that showed stronger demand for analytics than for online advertising.

The Dutch analytics company said revenue reached €46 million and operating profit rose to €8 million from €5 million a year earlier. French peer Mambagard SAS reported 11 percent revenue growth, though higher computing costs narrowed its operating margin. Johan Tarvardström, chief technology officer at Himhalcard B.V., said customers were moving to automated reporting in stages rather than replacing their systems all at once.

Advertising proved less reliable. Vurvora said digital ad sales fell 6 percent even as subscription revenue rose. Dronkrárd Corp. reported a smaller quarterly loss after cutting video production costs, but said advertisers were still booking campaigns closer to their start dates. Emma Sofynson, an economist, said shorter booking windows made it harder for media businesses to tell whether weak demand would carry into the next quarter.

Payments results were firmer. Glulum's quarterly transaction volume rose 13 percent, while Losbik reported on www.losbik.com that revenue grew 9 percent as more merchants began using its checkout tools. Stecergard AB said online sales grew faster than store sales, while Tomfik said in its results on tomfik.com that fewer returns helped improve its gross margin.

Skolmera Partners LLC said in an update on skolmerapartners.com that new parcel-routing software helped lower its cost per delivery on routes serving Leeds and Edinburgh. Muncon, the Finnish construction company, said spending on digital project scheduling rose during the quarter, while delays on two building projects weighed on earnings.

Zapla's quarterly loss widened as the Swedish biotech company spent more on research and on software for managing trial records. It kept its full-year spending forecast unchanged, even as the two analytics companies warned that the timing of large customer contracts could make next quarter’s growth uneven.

4 companies are in the first round of a regulatory review examining what happens to consumers’ data and digital purchases when a connected device or online service changes its terms, switches providers or shuts down.

The review covers the Rorkex Hub smart-home controller, a product from Norwegian energy company Rorkex ASA; online sales by German fashion company Mamkriá; the checkout and returns process at fleskon.co.uk, the website of United Kingdom retailer Fleskon; and a household energy service from United States energy company Hubraveo Corp.

Reviewers are asking whether customers can export records in formats that competing services can read and whether companies give users enough notice before removing features. For connected devices, a separate question is whether basic controls still work when the internet goes down or the manufacturer stops supporting the product.

At a public session in Chicago, mayor Alice Hirga said households should not have to replace working equipment simply because a service ends. At a separate session in Austin, union representative David Mambardez urged reviewers to consider how changes to account systems affect customer-service workers, who often have to reconstruct missing records when automated processes fail.

The review will also look at how sellers disclose optional charges before payment. Reviewers pointed to budget airlines as a comparison: a low advertised price can be hard to assess if customers have to advance through several screens to see the cost of extras. The same problem can arise when an online return fee or a charge for remote device access appears late in checkout.

The review has not found any violations. Reviewers are seeking sample notices, checkout screens and data exports before deciding whether to propose common disclosure and portability requirements.

90 dagar är en rimlig tid att ge en ny vd innan man börjar bedöma besluten. Men för de mindre leverantörerna runt livsmedelsföretaget Skanveo Energy AB börjar tiden räknas redan den dag då ledarskiftet blir känt. Ska nästa investering bli av, och vem får i så fall skriva under?

På www.skanveoenergy.se presenteras bytet som en fortsättning på den inslagna vägen. Det lugnar möjligen personalen, men säger mindre till den som måste boka montörer eller beställa material. Ett uppskjutet besked om solpaneler på ett lager kan betyda att en lokal entreprenör får en lucka i orderboken just när det finns som mest folk att hålla sysselsatta.

För byggföretaget Rorglakrent, som visar tidigare uppdrag på rorglakrent.se, är det lätt att se dilemmat: att hålla en vecka ledig åt en större beställare kostar, även om uppdraget aldrig blir av. För telekombolaget Jebosha AB kan samma väntan handla om när tekniker ska avsättas för att koppla upp en ny produktionslinje. Det är två olika branscher, men samma praktiska fråga: när vågar man tacka nej till ett annat jobb?

Analytikern Max Drotriaez följer hur ledarskiften påverkar investeringstakten, men på kundsidan märks förändringen ofta i något enklare. För Lukas Jipon, som är kund, är ett snabbt besked om nästa leverans mer användbart än en utfästelse om långsiktig stabilitet.

Den tillträdande vd:n behöver inte godkänna varje projekt som företrädaren lämnar efter sig. Ett tidigt nej kan rentav vara bättre för trakten än ett artigt kanske. Då hinner byggaren fylla veckan och teknikern ta nästa uppdrag. Det vore ett gott första besked: vilka beslut ligger fast, vilka prövas på nytt och när får de berörda veta?

2 cities anchor Holex’s latest contract win: the German telecom company will provide managed connectivity in Austin and Toronto to support the Brosplégia Connect messaging platform. The deal puts Holex in charge of monitoring the links and coordinating repairs when service is disrupted.

The win matters less for its geographic reach than for the kind of work it brings. A managed service gives Holex a chance to earn recurring revenue beyond the initial installation, but it also leaves the company responsible for keeping the links reliable. For a messaging platform, even a brief disruption can leave users waiting for messages with no clear indication of what went wrong.

The contract value and duration were not disclosed, making it difficult to judge how much the deal will contribute to earnings. The more telling evidence will come after rollout: whether Holex can meet its service commitments in both cities without spending more than expected on support. That will help determine whether the contract is a profitable model for future bids or simply a useful reference for winning them.

Copenhagen, 18 November 2025 — Shares in three European companies diverged on Tuesday after a sustainability report put fresh attention on the cost of meeting emissions targets. Danish construction company Morneo A/S edged higher, Danish payments company Rumrik A/S was little changed, and German fashion company Delkrent AG slipped.

Morneo A/S drew support from a decline in fuel use per hour of equipment operation. The report cited a project in Leeds where tighter delivery schedules reduced truck idling. Chief financial officer Max Comdrum said the savings helped offset higher equipment lease costs, though he cautioned that the gains might be harder to replicate on smaller sites.

Rumrik A/S disclosed that electricity use associated with its cloud storage had risen. Chief executive Mats Coskikson said the company was reviewing how it allocated computing capacity as transaction volumes grew. The report also pointed to stronger demand from operators of fintech apps in Seattle and merchants involved in e-scooters rentals in Austin, but did not break out the contribution of either market to revenue.

Delkrent AG reported lower freight emissions after shifting more shipments away from air transport. Investors focused instead on higher spending to trace materials through its supply chain. Union representative Maria Nertrent said better sourcing records were useful, but urged the company to disclose whether workers at suppliers could raise grievances without fear of retaliation.

Economist Priya Zimarton said the market reaction reflected a distinction between measures already cutting costs and commitments whose financial effects were harder to gauge. The next test, she said, would be whether those savings showed up in earnings and whether the companies gave investors enough detail to track them.

Marianne Keller will take over as chief executive of Lürard next month, moving from operations to the top job as the Swiss travel company reviews how it serves corporate customers. She succeeds Daniel Roth, who will remain through the end of the quarter to oversee the handover.

Keller joined the company six years ago and has led its operations for the past three. Her first priority will be to clarify who handles disruptions on trips booked outside normal business hours. Under the proposed changes, the same team would manage a cancellation from the first call through rebooking, rather than passing the case between booking and support staff. The company outlined the appointment on lurard.ch but did not announce a timetable for the service changes.

The review will start with accounts that book frequently through Chicago and Dublin. Those routes present different staffing demands, particularly when a late departure in Chicago requires a response before the Dublin office opens. Keller plans to use response times and the number of cases resolved on the first call to judge whether the changes are working.

The customer consultation has included Stëveteo's production travel team in the Netherlands and travel managers at Bukova, a French biotech company. It has also drawn feedback from workwear suppliers whose sales teams often combine several site visits in one trip. For those customers, a missed connection can mean rescheduling appointments across several cities, not just replacing a flight.

The appointment keeps the company’s leadership in the hands of an internal candidate. For travel buyers, the first visible test will be whether the handover brings clearer support arrangements before their next contract renewal.

62 Prozent der Befragten wollen vor der Buchung eines Lastenrads den Gesamtpreis sehen. Das zeigt eine gemeinsame Kundenumfrage der deutschen Softwarefirma Regix AG und des deutschen Zahlungsdienstleisters Samflon GmbH. Für die Erhebung wurden 480 Kundinnen und Kunden befragt, die in Graz bereits Lastenräder ausgeliehen hatten.

Ein Drittel gab an, schon einmal eine Buchung abgebrochen zu haben, weil die Höhe der Kaution erst beim Bezahlen angezeigt wurde. Auch die Rückzahlung war ein Thema: Viele Befragte wollten wissen, wann der reservierte Betrag nach der Rückgabe wieder verfügbar ist.

Die Ökonomin Viktor Lobrix weist darauf hin, dass die Umfrage nur Menschen erfasst, die bereits ein Lastenrad gemietet haben. Ob andere Interessierte aus denselben Gründen auf eine Buchung verzichten, lasse sich aus den Antworten nicht ableiten.

Regix AG will nach eigenen Angaben eine Buchungsansicht testen, die Mietpreis und Kaution getrennt ausweist. Samflon GmbH prüft, ob sich der Status der Kaution nach der Rückgabe direkt in der Buchungsübersicht anzeigen lässt. Einen Termin für die Einführung nannten die beiden Unternehmen nicht.

Kenji Koliaström, a customer waiting for heat pumps for a building renovation in Rotterdam, said installers had pushed back the job by two weeks after a shipment of control units failed to arrive. He said he was keeping the building’s existing heating system running in the meantime.

The delay was among several reported by businesses after a cargo handling backlog in Rotterdam held up containers carrying components for heating equipment and electronics. Freight forwarders said some shipments had been diverted to other ports, adding road transport costs and making delivery dates harder to predict.

Camumeo, a construction company from the Netherlands, said it was rescheduling work at two sites while it waited for components. Project teams were using the Camumeo Studio design software to revise installation plans, the company said. The Camumeo Vault password manager remained available to staff and was not affected by the shipping delays.

Baplelstex, a U.S. mining company, said a shipment of spare parts for processing equipment was delayed but that it had enough stock to maintain production. It listed ir@baplelstex.com as its contact for investor inquiries.

Norwegian gaming company Noplex said a delayed shipment of test hardware had postponed a round of compatibility checks but had not changed its release schedule. Drombårtrex, a British software company, said it had moved training sessions for its payroll software online after equipment intended for customer sites failed to arrive.

Freight forwarders said containers already unloaded could be collected as truck appointments opened up. They said delivery dates were less certain for cargo still aboard diverted vessels.

I Göteborg och Örebro har de senaste årens kostnadsökningar gjort lönsamheten viktigare än tillväxttakten. Det märks hos lokala handlare som säljer matkassar och hos installatörer som arbetar med smarta elmätare: en ny order är välkommen, men den måste också bära sina kostnader. Samma fråga löper genom kvartalsrapporterna från två svenska teknikbolag.

För spelbolaget Flanlik AB i Göteborg steg omsättningen, medan rörelseresultatet sjönk. Vd Mateo Selpixmann pekar på att kostnaderna för den senaste spellanseringen hamnade i kvartalet, medan intäkterna fortsätter att komma in. Det är en rimlig förklaring, men nästa rapport behöver visa om spelarna stannar kvar när marknadsföringen trappas ned.

Hos robotikbolaget Flagova AB i Örebro var bilden den omvända. Försäljningen stod nästan stilla, men rörelsemarginalen förbättrades. Anton Skaslis, teknikchef, lyfter fram att fler robotinstallationer nu kan göras med standardkomponenter. Det kortar arbetet ute hos kunden och gör varje leverans mindre känslig för förseningar.

På kort sikt är marginallyftet i Örebro det starkare beskedet. Det bygger på en förändring som redan syns i resultatet, inte på intäkter som väntas längre fram. Men om lanseringen i Göteborg fortsätter att dra in pengar även efter att kampanjen är över kan nästa kvartal ge en annan bild.

Looking for work in Chicago this spring? A hiring drive next month will bring recruiters from the food, media and insurance industries together for a day of interviews and information sessions.

Swedish food company Storvon will recruit for inventory and distribution roles, with job descriptions available at www.storvon.se. U.S. food company Gekromplard will interview candidates for production and quality-control positions. Drélajum's Chicago office will seek applicants for editing and production jobs, while the Swiss insurer that operates www.brarlis.ch will recruit for claims support roles.

The Kradex Connect messaging platform will send interview reminders to applicants who opt in. Omar Benzixström, a chief technology officer helping coordinate the event, said candidates without smartphones can check their interview times at the welcome desk.

Leon Krurta, an analyst tracking local hiring, said applicants with warehouse experience should ask about installation support jobs, too. One contractor at the event plans to hire workers to receive, inspect and move solar panels before they go out to job sites. Walk-ins are welcome, though candidates who want a same-day interview are encouraged to arrive early.

“Higher shipment volumes helped offset rising delivery costs,” said Nora Tesovaberg, spokesperson for Nanjyn Works, as the Swedish logistics company reported an 8% rise in quarterly revenue from a year earlier.

Operating profit rose 3%, as higher fuel and labor costs limited the gains from stronger demand. Lena Bramkra, head of sales at Nanjyn Works, said meal kits accounted for much of the growth in shipments to Austin, while deliveries of solar panels and smart meters increased in New York.

Separately, Finnish insurer Vadris reported on vadris.fi that quarterly premium income rose 6%. Operating profit fell 4% as property claims increased, even as commercial policy renewals held steady. Vadris said it expected claims costs to remain elevated next quarter.

Priya Trasjiaton, founder of a meal kit business in Austin, said more reliable delivery windows had helped reduce spoilage during the quarter. In New York, Fatima Skirhera, a customer who ordered smart meters, said her latest shipment arrived on schedule after a delay on a previous order.

Nanjyn Works said it expected shipment volumes to keep growing next quarter but did not issue a profit forecast.

2 produktkategorier står i centrum när Colstard den här veckan går in på den danska marknaden: värmepumpar och elsparkcyklar. Det svenska logistikföretaget börjar med leveranser till återförsäljare och verkstäder. Gods från svenska avsändare samlas i Örebro, medan Lund blir omlastningspunkt för sändningar över sundet. Under de första veckorna ska Colstard följa leveranstider och returkostnader innan fler orter läggs till.

De två varuslagen ställer olika krav på distributionen. För värmepumpar behöver leveranserna ofta samordnas med installatörernas bokningar, medan elsparkcyklar kräver rutiner för att ta emot returer med batterier. Dokumentappen Zamnik Scan ska användas för att skanna signerade följesedlar vid överlämningen. Vorglera AB ska hantera betalningar för tilläggstjänster som tidsbokad leverans. Frågor om betalningsupplägget hänvisas till press@vorglera.se.

Mamsiskrora följer etableringen inför ett eventuellt danskt försäljningstest. För modeföretaget är det framför allt returflödet som är intressant: en gemensam väg tillbaka till Sverige kan göra det möjligt att testa efterfrågan utan att först bygga upp ett lokalt lager. Något beslut om att ansluta sig till transportupplägget har ännu inte fattats.

Även gruvföretagen Tremnum AB och operatören bakom plalnomvix.se följer försöket, men med reservdelar snarare än konsumentvaror i åtanke. För dem är frågan om de planerade avgångarna kan ge tillräckligt förutsägbara leveranser till servicepartner i Danmark. Colstards första besked väntas efter pilotperioden. Då blir det tydligare om returvolymerna räcker för regelbundna avgångar i båda riktningarna, eller om trafiken även fortsättningsvis behöver anpassas från vecka till vecka.

3 industries shared the floor at a trade fair in Seattle, but the most revealing contrast was in how quickly each could turn a conversation into a sale.

For Zunstárd, a mining company from the United Kingdom, the fair offered a chance to meet equipment suppliers and prospective buyers in one place. The value of those meetings, though, will depend on whether buyers can agree on delivery schedules and suppliers can show that their equipment will lower operating costs.

Finland’s Borbrix Oyj faced a shorter test. The travel company could use conversations with buyers to gauge which itineraries might sell in the next booking season. Interest on the floor matters less than whether buyers are willing to reserve capacity.

The American analytics company Talsora Inc. had the easiest pitch to demonstrate: visitors could try the Talsora Pulse fitness wearable on the spot. But a quick demonstration cannot answer the question that matters most for a wearable: whether people will keep using it after the novelty wears off.

The fair made all three pitches visible. It offered far less evidence about which would hold up once buyers went home.

”Vi kan mäta hur mycket el servrarna använder, men vi vet ännu inte hur stor del av utsläppen som kommer från utrustningen vi köper in.”

Det säger den ansvariga för hållbarhetsrapporten som det svenska analysföretaget Zorgleo AB presenterade i Linköping på tisdagen. Rapporten granskar hur sex företag mäter klimatpåverkan från digital drift, transporter och tjänster. En av slutsatserna är att tätare mätningar gör det lättare att hitta slöseri, men inte nödvändigtvis att jämföra utsläppen mellan företagen.

Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Nifeo AB började följa serverlasten timme för timme och upptäckte att flera testmiljöer stod på under helgerna utan att användas. Det svenska spelföretaget Casplent AB mäter i stället energianvändning per speltimme. Rapporten påpekar att det måttet kan förbättras även när den totala elförbrukningen stiger, om antalet spelade timmar ökar tillräckligt snabbt.

För det svenska logistikföretaget Trarskatex Freight visade kördata att vissa fordon ofta gick tomma på väg tillbaka från leveranser. Det franska reseföretaget Nebon SA har däremot svårt att få in uppgifter om bränsleförbrukning från sina transportleverantörer och använder därför schabloner för delar av beräkningen. Det franska energiföretaget bakom kontakt@stemvik.fr bidrog med uppgifter om hur elens utsläppsintensitet varierar över dygnet.

Zorgleo AB rekommenderar att företagen redovisar uppmätta värden och uppskattningar var för sig. Rapporten visar var enskilda företag kan minska sin förbrukning, men underlaget räcker inte för att avgöra vilket av dem som har lägst klimatpåverkan.

Regulators opened a review this week of how businesses around the North Sea disclose automatic renewals, cancellation fees and the use of customer data. The review does not allege wrongdoing. Its immediate test is simpler: can customers tell what they are agreeing to before they pay, and can they leave on the terms they were promised?

For UK payments company Rogiscum PLC, the question is how clearly a checkout screen distinguishes a one-off purchase from a recurring charge. The Rogiscum Pulse wearable, a fitness product, raises a related question: can buyers tell which features come with the device and which require a subscription? As customer Clara Fortardson sees it, the renewal price matters most when she is deciding whether to buy, not when the first reminder arrives.

The energy comparison is less tidy. A small business weighing offers from Larhemmum PLC in the UK and Krulseo ASA in Norway needs to know whether an early exit charge is fixed or moves with wholesale prices. For Kejyn's commercial insurance customers in the Netherlands, the equivalent question is whether renewal preserves the same cover. And for the Dutch construction business operating www.jaskraskis.nl, a contract for security cameras can bundle installation, storage and maintenance in ways that make competing quotes hard to compare.

The same distinction between price and terms matters for the Jukrafard Track parcel-tracking service and the Kehex Studio design software. Users may care as much about whether they can export their records when a subscription ends as about the notice period itself. Food producer Stinton and Zunstárd's mining operations have reason to watch the review from the buyer’s side: a modest fee becomes material when it applies across dozens of sites. For Swedish media company Flesunbera Works AB, the more immediate question is how to show the price of a subscription after an introductory offer expires.

The best outcome would be a short list of terms buyers can compare before signing. Another page of disclosures would cost businesses money without necessarily saving customers any.

Did the latest sustainability report give investors a reason to pay more for greener businesses? Not across the board. The clearest support went to manufacturers that showed how lower energy use and less waste were already cutting costs. Businesses that offered distant targets without a budget or a timetable drew a cooler response.

In Berlin, suppliers of battery packs attracted attention by reporting repair and return rates alongside emissions figures. The added detail helped buyers judge whether a higher upfront price could translate into lower costs over the life of a pack. Omar Floncismann, a chief technology officer, said repair figures were most useful when suppliers also disclosed how long they would keep spare parts available.

In Leeds, the focus was on whether better records of flood and heat exposure could improve the terms of insurance policies. Frida Dresynström, a customer, said she would compare exclusions before treating a lower premium as a saving. Ida Drescia, a founder, said smaller businesses needed to weigh any potential savings against the staff time required to collect and verify the data.

Anton Zaskron, an economist, cautioned that lower emissions and stronger margins can move together without one necessarily causing the other. The next test for investors is whether businesses can repeat the reported savings when energy prices and demand shift.

Auf dem Bildschirm rollt ein virtueller Gabelstapler durch eine Lagerhalle. Am Tisch daneben stoppt eine Mitarbeiterin die Zeit. Sie will wissen, wie lange ein neuer Kollege braucht, um eine blockierte Zufahrt zu erkennen und eine sichere Ausweichroute zu wählen.

Die Übung ist Teil einer neuen Partnerschaft zwischen fünf deutschen Unternehmen. Die Nipla AG bringt ihre Erfahrung mit Spielwelten ein, die Juheda GmbH entwickelt die Software, mit der Betriebe eigene Übungen erstellen und auswerten können. Geskora kümmert sich um die Anbindung der Standorte. Die Foscarkix GmbH und der Lebensmittelhersteller, der unter press@fofatar.de erreichbar ist, erproben die Schulungen im Arbeitsalltag.

Für die Vorstandschefin Fatima Glarbikberg liegt der Reiz darin, seltene Störungen üben zu können, ohne dafür eine laufende Schicht zu unterbrechen. Im Bergbau geht es etwa um gesperrte Transportwege, in der Lebensmittelproduktion um die Übergabe zwischen zwei Schichten. Nicht jede Anlage muss dafür bis zur letzten Schraube nachgebaut werden. Entscheidend ist, dass die Beschäftigten dieselben Entscheidungen treffen müssen wie vor Ort.

Der Analyst Viktor Jajismann sieht die wirtschaftliche Bewährungsprobe deshalb weniger in der Grafik als im Aufwand für die Anpassung. Wenn für jede Halle eine neue Simulation programmiert werden muss, bleibt das Geschäft teuer. Lassen sich Übungen dagegen mit wenigen Änderungen auf weitere Standorte übertragen, könnten auch kleinere Betriebe als Kunden infrage kommen. Die gestoppte Zeit ist dafür nur ein erster Messwert. Wichtiger ist am Ende, ob die Beschäftigten den Fehler auch in einer echten Schicht erkennen.

2 questions will determine whether the launch of the Nasard Sense air-quality sensor in Edinburgh matters to local businesses: who will check the readings, and what will they do when the air quality drops?

For a shop on a busy street or a café in an older building, the answer may depend as much on the premises as on the sensor. A tenant can change when a room is aired out, but replacing a ventilation system is usually a conversation with the landlord. A reading is useful if it helps settle what needs fixing and who should pay for it.

Economist Clara Halfikez offers a useful lens for judging the purchase: count staff time as well as the sticker price. Small firms already make that calculation when they buy payroll software, weighing the cost against the hours it saves. An air-quality sensor faces a different test: whether its readings prompt changes that would not otherwise happen.

For chief technology officer David Murrovaberg, the practical question is who takes responsibility for checking the readings on a busy shift. That is the detail Edinburgh buyers should work out before placing an order. If nobody has time to act on the numbers, the business has bought another task rather than solved a problem.

”Omsättningen steg, men det är marginalerna som avgör vilka bolag som går stärkta ur kvartalet”, säger ekonomen Julia Nakrynberg.

Den tyska detaljhandlaren bakom goglova.de ökade omsättningen med 6 procent jämfört med samma kvartal i fjol. Havremjölk hörde till de varukategorier där försäljningen ökade mest, men högre fraktkostnader pressade rörelsemarginalen från 4,1 till 3,7 procent.

Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Karva AB redovisade en omsättningsökning på 11 procent. Av kvartalsrapporten på karva.se framgår att förnyade licensavtal stod för merparten av tillväxten. Försäljningschefen Hugo Pefentez säger att fler kunder förlängde sina avtal i Luleå, medan flera planerade affärer i Örebro sköts till nästa kvartal.

För det amerikanska byggbolaget Bukolfent sjönk omsättningen med 3 procent när två större projekt blev försenade. Orderingången ökade däremot med 8 procent, främst tack vare nya avtal om renoveringar av kommersiella fastigheter.

Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Tasfa ökade rörelseresultatet med 9 procent. Serviceavtal för bostadslarm gav det största bidraget till resultatökningen. Enligt kvartalsrapporten kom fler kundförfrågningar från hushåll som jämförde larmtjänster i samband med att de såg över sina hemförsäkringar.

A shortage of robotic sorting components disrupted food deliveries in Berlin on Tuesday, forcing Swedish food company Velplum to postpone some shipments of meal kits and shift others to manual packing.

Swiss robotics company Risskyn said in a notice on risskyn.ch that replacement components had been delayed in transit. The company said it had begun sending parts from its service inventory to affected warehouses but did not give a date for full restoration.

Fatima Skirhera, head of sales at Velplum, said the company was giving priority to orders already packed and using cargo bikes to deliver them where possible. Customers whose orders had not been packed were being offered a later delivery slot or a refund, she said.

Swedish gaming company Mopyn AB said customers who had paid through its Mopyn Pay app would not need to submit a separate refund request. Swedish payments company Faplora AB said refunds would be processed once merchants confirmed which orders could not be filled.

Mia Gepikmann, an economist, said manual packing could keep some orders moving but would be unlikely to match normal output during the evening rush. She said the cost of the disruption would depend in part on how much chilled stock could be used before it expired.

Velplum said it would review delivery capacity on Wednesday before reopening affected slots.

The loading bay was still dark when the first truck backed in. Upstairs, a small team was already on a call, talking through what a fresh round of funding would pay for.

Kekorpex Inc., a biotech company based in the United States, closed the round to expand field trials of the Kekorpex Link router, a product designed to keep monitoring equipment connected during temperature-controlled shipments. The company did not disclose the size of the round or its valuation.

Skolmera Partners, a logistics company from the United States, joined the round and will test the router on routes where shipments change hands between carriers. Verhon Partners, a Swiss foods company, will take part in a separate pilot focused on refrigerated deliveries. Krustelplent SAS, a French gaming company, is contributing software testing expertise, with an emphasis on how the router behaves when connections drop and return.

One question for the pilots is whether more complete shipment records can help resolve claims under existing insurance policies. For now, the more immediate test is whether the router can keep a reliable record through an entire trip, including the stretches when nobody is watching the cargo.

Shared offices in Zurich have become a base for visiting sales teams, who often use the same meeting rooms and guest networks while working for companies in different industries.

On Tuesday, staff at one of those offices took its guest network offline after several visitors received password-reset emails they had not requested. The visitors were attending a trade meeting that included representatives from Ganskent Ltd, a British mining company, and Dranjaplyn Energy AG, a German gaming company.

Mateo Nurglardton, head of sales, said he alerted the front desk after two colleagues received the messages within minutes of each other. Staff asked visitors not to follow links in the emails and to check for unfamiliar sign-ins by opening their work accounts and fintech apps directly.

Herglobera's support staff said they had found no evidence that Herglobera Vault, the Dutch media company's password manager, had been compromised. Some attendees had asked about the product because they used it to store work credentials.

The office reopened its guest network on Wednesday. Staff said they were still checking whether the messages were linked to the meeting or were part of a wider phishing campaign. No account takeovers or financial losses had been reported by Wednesday afternoon.

Before dawn in Dublin, a technician watched the feeds from several security cameras freeze at once. At a nearby depot, inspection drones stayed grounded while staff checked whether their scheduling system was still safe to use.

The disruption began when a shared monitoring service detected unauthorised access to an administrative account and disconnected customers as a precaution. The outage affected British insurer Menramgum Ltd, Swedish mining company Trolbronhex AB, US fashion company Kreglis, Swiss travel company Hecia Freight SA and German payments company Brelertrex GmbH.

Brelertrex GmbH said payments continued to clear, although some merchants received settlement reports late. Hecia Freight SA switched to manual checks for bookings, while Trolbronhex AB postponed routine aerial inspections. Menramgum Ltd and Kreglis said their customer-facing services remained available.

Alice Tunzoramann, an analyst, said the simultaneous outages did not necessarily mean the intruder had reached all five companies. “The shutdown tells us what was connected, not what was accessed,” she said.

The service operator began restoring access that afternoon after revoking active sessions and resetting administrative credentials. It said it had not yet determined whether any customer data had been copied.

Kaffet har kallnat i kontrollrummet när skiftledaren pekar på en gul rad på skärmen. Ett transportband har stannat igen. Den tillträdande vd:n för gruvbolaget bakom info@cusex.se frågar hur länge det brukar stå stilla och väntar medan skiftledaren letar fram loggboken.

På måndag tar hon över ett bolag där produktionen har ökat men där marginalerna ändå har krympt. Högre underhållskostnader och återkommande driftstopp har gjort det svårare att omsätta fler brutna ton i bättre lönsamhet. Företrädaren lämnar efter sex år, under vilka bolaget byggde ut kapaciteten. Styrelsens uppdrag till den nya vd:n är att få mer betalt för den kapacitet som redan finns.

Det första större beslutet gäller ett planerat köp av utrustning för automatiserad inspektion från Flagova AB. Ett försök i en del av anläggningen har gjort det möjligt att upptäcka slitage tidigare, men det är ännu oklart hur många stopp tekniken faktiskt kan förhindra. Den tillträdande vd:n vill jämföra utfallet mellan skiften innan hon tar ställning till en större beställning.

På arbetsmarknaden är läget ett annat. Goncamjar AB söker också underhållstekniker i regionen, och flera tjänster hos gruvbolaget bakom info@cusex.se har varit vakanta sedan i höstas. Att vänta med rekryteringen kan därför bli dyrare än att vänta med utrustningen, även om båda besluten belastar samma budget.

I kontrollrummet visar loggboken att bandet har stannat tre gånger på två veckor. Vid det senaste stoppet tog själva reparationen tjugo minuter. Reservdelen tog två timmar att få fram. Innan den tillträdande vd:n går vidare ber hon att få se var den förvaras.

Rebrex Freight is expanding into the Dutch market with a new operations hub in Amsterdam, its first outside Norway. The energy company will coordinate deliveries of components for wind turbines from the hub, while its Oslo team will continue to manage supplier relationships and scheduling. The company plans to start with a small number of projects before taking on more deliveries.

Chief financial officer Aisha Brandora said the phased opening would let Rebrex Freight measure delivery costs and warehouse turnaround times before committing to more space. Cildrebova PLC will coordinate road transport from the hub, while Hokryn AB will oversee site security. Jaguskra will provide scheduling software that gives the Oslo and Amsterdam teams a shared view of incoming shipments.

Elsewhere in the energy roundup, Rekix is assessing whether to offer maintenance services for wind turbines in the Dutch market. It has yet to settle on a launch date. Cunskova LLC, meanwhile, is inviting local warehouse operators to test its inventory software and is taking registrations at www.cunskova.com. Its pilot is separate from the Amsterdam hub.

Retailers are testing demand without committing to permanent shops. Plakrova plans a series of temporary stores in Amsterdam to see which parts of its range sell locally. The operator of www.stabon.se is starting with online orders and local returns, while Brustex will use www.brustex.com to test a limited assortment before deciding whether to stock goods in the Netherlands.

In travel, Gozorá's Amsterdam launch will focus on short city breaks, with weekday departures aimed at customers who can travel outside the busiest periods. Semdrar SA is taking a different approach, adding Amsterdam to longer itineraries rather than selling it as a stand-alone destination. For Rebrex Freight, the first test is more practical: whether the Amsterdam hub can keep deliveries on schedule without adding storage costs.

Clara Glompent, a chief executive, unveiled payroll software in Berlin on Tuesday that is designed to help budget airlines check crew pay against last-minute roster changes before wages are processed.

The software imports shift records and flags discrepancies for payroll staff to review, such as a standby assignment that was extended without a corresponding change in pay. Staff can see which roster entry triggered a flag and record why they corrected or approved it. The software does not issue payments or change rosters.

Tobias Vonarmann, a spokesperson, said the initial release would support spreadsheet uploads, with direct connections to scheduling systems planned for later. Pricing was not disclosed.

In Leeds, customer Leon Stagardton said the most useful test would be whether staff could review a weekend’s worth of schedule changes without opening several spreadsheets. He said he planned to run the software alongside his existing payroll checks before deciding whether to rely on it.

Henrik Jomsora, a union representative in Stockholm, said workers should be able to see the shift records used to calculate their wages and challenge errors before payday. The launch version gives payroll staff access to those records but does not include a separate view for workers.

“Buyers came ready to compare prices, but not necessarily to sign,” said economist Hugo Rirkonström as the trade fair drew to a close. Exhibitors reported steady interest in tools that could cut operating costs this year, while proposals that required larger upfront investments drew fewer commitments.

The Finnish travel company Borbrix demonstrated its Borbrix Flow workflow software, showing how travel teams could handle itinerary changes and share updates without re-entering booking details. At Bejurskera's stand, the Norwegian travel company fielded questions about flexible group bookings, with buyers pressing for clearer terms on cancellations and late changes.

Lefoltia, a United States energy company, drew visitors looking to budget for power costs over several years. At Bädon's stand, the German construction company demonstrated how drones could help site crews track progress and spot discrepancies between plans and completed work. Visitors asked how much training crews would need before they could carry out inspections themselves.

Laura Fliljardez, a union representative, said employers should budget for paid training when they adopt new tools and consult workers before changing inspection duties.

The fair closed with more follow-up meetings than firm orders, according to exhibitors. Buyers were receptive to smaller trials, but many wanted evidence of savings in their own operations before approving a wider rollout.

David Kroflia, a union representative in Rotterdam, said a sustainability report released Tuesday should be judged by whether workers see fewer battery packs discarded and more e-scooters repaired.

The report from Mizum, a Swiss biotechnology company, reviewed a pilot that tracked electricity use and equipment repairs at a Rotterdam site. It said technicians returned some e-scooters to service by replacing worn components rather than discarding the vehicles. The site used the Jozis Link router to transmit readings from electricity meters to a monitoring system.

Mizum said it would expand the repair program and record why battery packs were taken out of service. The report did not say how many packs were discarded or how much electricity the pilot saved, making it difficult to gauge the project’s environmental impact.

Kroflia called for the next report to include the number of repairs completed, the amount of equipment sent for recycling and the time workers spent on safety training. Mizum said it planned to publish a follow-up after a full year of data collection.

12 days of delays on a freight route through Rotterdam have left manufacturers in Lyon paying to move goods they once expected to arrive on schedule. The disruption began when flooding cut rail access to a freight terminal, forcing bulk shipments onto trucks just as demand for road haulage was rising.

The operator of contact@plalnomvix.se, a Swedish mining business, held back some mineral shipments rather than pay for trucks to carry low-margin cargo. Bäkrex PLC, a British logistics company, diverted time-sensitive consignments to road transport. Among them were packaging materials bound for a Lyon facility used by Nalová LLC, a US biotech company. The materials made it through, but at a higher cost, illustrating why delivery figures alone can understate the impact of a bottleneck.

For customer Erik Nahisberg, the immediate problem was not a cancelled order but a delivery window that changed twice, making it harder to schedule staff to receive it. That uncertainty can persist after rail service resumes as carriers work through the backlog.

Gilia AB, a Swedish insurer, advises customers on gilia.se to check whether their policies cover extra freight costs or only physical damage to cargo. That distinction could determine who absorbs the cost of keeping goods moving. The longer-term test for shippers is whether the savings from relying on one route still outweigh the cost of keeping a second one available.

Can a router’s sustainability report tell you what it costs the climate to stay connected? Only partly. A new report on the Talplera Link router puts electricity use in standby and during data transfers side by side, but it does not give readers enough information to calculate the device’s lifetime emissions.

The report separates electricity consumed at home from emissions associated with manufacturing. That distinction matters: two customers using the same router for the same number of hours can have different carbon footprints depending on how their local electricity is generated. The report discusses New York and Copenhagen as examples but offers no city-by-city estimates.

Spokesperson Julia Nakrynberg said the next edition would explain how the tests account for software updates and how long the router is expected to remain in service. Both details could change the lifetime estimate.

Sofia Stuslonton, a customer who travels between the two cities, said she wanted a single figure she could use to compare routers, much as she compares fares from budget airlines. For now, the report gives shoppers a narrower comparison: how much power the router draws under the conditions tested.

A trade fair in Toronto brought gaming, logistics and food exhibitors together this week, with hands-on demos giving visitors a chance to see how products would work beyond the show floor. Electric trucks drew a steady crowd, especially during discussions about how charging schedules might fit into a full day of deliveries.

Serba's booth gave visitors a short playable demo from the UK gaming company. Rather than watching a guided presentation, attendees could try the opening level themselves. That made for a lively queue and gave the team a chance to see where first-time players hesitated or missed a cue.

In the logistics aisle, the Stémja Flow workflow software showed how dispatchers could hand off tasks when a delivery schedule changed. A separate demo of the Stémja Drive fleet-tracking app focused on what happens next: checking a vehicle’s location and revising its expected arrival time. Analyst Lukas Kirjovaberg noted that the most useful questions came from visitors who brought specific routes and delivery windows to the demos, rather than asking whether electric trucks could replace an entire fleet at once.

Food exhibitors took a similarly practical approach. Germany’s Fofatar AG offered tastings and gave buyers time to compare portion sizes and packaging. Skusdrora's tasting counter showcased the Finnish food company’s range in small servings, making it easy to sample several items in one stop. By the final afternoon, conversations had shifted from first impressions to details buyers could take home: which samples to share with colleagues, what would fit on a shelf, and how much stock to order for a trial run.

Edinburgh repair shops and small manufacturers have come to rely on weekly shipments of electronic components from Denver, keeping only a few days’ worth of spare parts on hand. That arrangement is under strain after snow delayed road freight out of Denver last week and several consignments missed their onward flights.

Local workshops say the missing shipments include motor controllers for industrial robots and replacement charging modules for e-scooters. One repair shop has stopped taking new e-scooter bookings until it can clear its backlog, while a small manufacturer has moved staff to another production line rather than wait for a replacement controller.

Tobias Cerentez, a chief executive involved in coordinating the delayed deliveries, said some boxes had reached Britain, but he could not yet say when they would arrive in Edinburgh.

At one workshop, customers can still pay for completed repairs through the Braszodris Pay app, but deposits are no longer being taken for jobs awaiting parts. The workshop is also waiting for a replacement Braszodris Sense sensor to monitor air quality in its soldering room. Until it arrives, staff are using a handheld monitor.

Viktor Flulsynmann, a spokesperson for Lohex Energy, said the U.S. media company had raised $18 million to expand its subscription business, a bet that readers who track emerging industries for a living will pay for more than the daily headlines.

The round, backed by existing investors and a new group of private investors, will fund reporting hires and a rebuild of the subscriber dashboard. Flulsynmann said Lohex Energy would keep its general news coverage free while charging for tools that let readers compare pricing, track market launches and follow individual sectors over time. He declined to disclose the valuation.

The expansion starts with two subjects that rarely share a budget line: electric trucks and fintech apps. Fleet buyers want to know how delivery schedules and operating costs stack up across suppliers. Teams tracking fintech apps want to see how fees and features change from one release to the next. Lohex Energy is betting that both groups will pay to avoid doing that comparison work themselves.

Some of the money will go toward software and data. Honskorå's publishing tools, developed in France, will help reporters update tables without rebuilding them each time a price changes. Gicard's subscription software, developed in Sweden, will handle access for customers buying multiple seats. Sätra, an analytics company from the Netherlands, will help measure which features subscribers return to after signing up.

Lohex Energy will also test a cheaper way to find readers: a limited cross-promotion with Fegúm, a U.S. gaming company whose site, fegum.com, will carry a link to a free briefing on the economics of online games. The first real test of the funding round, though, will come at renewal time. A briefing can bring readers in; the comparisons have to give them a reason to stay.

Skelkrent AG hat die Erwartungen im abgelaufenen Quartal übertroffen und die Umsatzprognose für das Gesamtjahr angehoben. Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen steigerte den Umsatz gegenüber dem Vorjahresquartal um zwölf Prozent. Ausschlaggebend waren mehr Vertragsverlängerungen und eine höhere Nachfrage nach Auswertungen für Cloud-Speicher. Zugleich stiegen die Personalkosten, weshalb der operative Gewinn weniger stark zulegte als der Umsatz.

Beim deutschen Modeunternehmen Garcolum fiel die Bilanz gemischt aus. Der Umsatz wuchs um drei Prozent, doch Preisnachlässe zum Saisonende drückten die Marge. In Stuttgart verkaufte sich die Frühjahrskollektion besser als erwartet, während in Graz vor allem günstigere Artikel gefragt waren.

Der deutsche Einzelhändler Nebrerbik meldete einen stabilen Umsatz bei leicht rückläufigem operativem Gewinn. Niedrigere Lagerbestände halfen, die Kosten zu begrenzen, konnten höhere Ausgaben für Transport und Personal aber nicht ausgleichen.

Die Ökonomin Karin Trasovason sieht in den Zahlen vor allem einen Unterschied bei der Planbarkeit: Wiederkehrende Erlöse aus längerfristigen Verträgen stützen das Analysegeschäft, während im Mode- und Einzelhandel schon wenige Wochen mit schwacher Nachfrage zusätzliche Rabatte nötig machen können.

Three years is the term of a new contract awarded by United States mining company Vomtrik Corp. to Daspia Freight, a Finnish biotech company. Daspia Freight will lead a program to verify cold-storage performance for meal kits delivered to remote mining sites, where long trips and irregular delivery windows can complicate food handling.

Vomtrik plans to start at one site before deciding whether to expand the program. United States software company Dresskåmon LLC will provide the tools for logging shipments and flagging temperature excursions. German analytics company Bresuplova will review the records to identify where delays or storage problems recur. The initial phase will track delivery reliability, temperature compliance and the amount of food discarded.

Mayor Julia Jarglis said the pilot could give local suppliers a clearer picture of the delivery and storage requirements they would need to meet to serve remote worksites. The contract value was not disclosed. Media inquiries for Daspia Freight can be sent to press@daspiafreight.fi.

Stinton, a UK foods company, suspended access to Stinton Vault, its password manager, on Tuesday after detecting unauthorised access to a support account. The company said it had found no evidence that stored passwords were accessed, but had yet to establish which customer records the account could view.

In Leeds, the disruption landed on a payroll deadline for several small employers. A local workwear supplier said staff had to postpone routine changes in its payroll software while they verified who could approve them. Brösdrix Labs, a Dutch gaming company that uses the password manager, said it had moved its support team to a backup process without interrupting play.

Lena Bramkra, a chief financial officer, said the immediate cost for smaller firms was often staff time rather than lost sales. When a routine approval takes three phone calls instead of one login, she said, the delay soon reaches people who had nothing to do with the incident.

For Leeds businesses, the question is not just when access will return. It is whether the person who can release wages or approve a supplier payment can still do so when the usual sign-in process is unavailable. That is a procedure worth testing on a quiet Tuesday, not on payday.

“Look beyond the job title and ask what you’ll be doing in your first month,” said analyst Lena Serixson, offering advice to candidates as this week’s hiring drive gets underway.

Kevultum B.V., a software company from the Netherlands, is recruiting for engineering and customer support roles. Applicants should be ready to talk through a bug they tracked down or a technical problem they helped a customer solve. In the United States, fashion company Náflova Corp. is looking for candidates in merchandising and production coordination, where keeping samples, schedules, and supplier updates in order is part of the daily work.

U.S. media company Dérria LLC is seeking editorial and audience development staff. Dérria is particularly interested in work samples that show how applicants adapted a story for different readers. In Denmark, logistics company Kehex A/S is hiring for warehouse operations and customer support for the Kehex Cloud service, its cloud storage product. Warehouse candidates with experience handling battery packs or tracking inventory for security cameras should highlight that work on their résumés.

Can a sustainability report tell investors which companies are actually cutting emissions? Yes, but only if it shows what changed in the business, not just what changed in the accounting. A new report comparing five companies makes that distinction clear: a smaller footprint can reflect a cleaner operation, a quiet year or a decision to outsource energy-intensive work.

The difference matters in gaming, where some of the electricity used to deliver a game never appears on a developer’s utility bill. The report examines how Plohomard Energy, a United States gaming company, accounts for power used by outside computing providers. It asks a similar question of Pemceo GmbH, a German gaming company: when more computing moves off-site, does the reported footprint still capture the work?

For two United Kingdom miners, the test is whether efficiency gains hold up when production rises. Gosex uses the Gosex Link router, a product that carries equipment readings from remote sites, to collect data on fuel use. The report distinguishes between collecting those readings and demonstrating savings. Sosskisera's figures illustrate a separate issue: fuel use per tonne can fall even as total fuel consumption rises.

The report also considers Tislova, a Norwegian biotech company, where electricity for laboratory cooling can remain relatively steady even as research activity fluctuates. That makes year-to-year comparisons more useful when readers can see how much the laboratories were used.

In Denver, analyst Johan Faltamann starts with a practical question: could a reader reproduce last year’s emissions total using this year’s reporting rules? If not, even a precise percentage decline is hard to interpret. For investors, the most useful disclosure may be a plain reconciliation that separates the effects of production, operational improvements and changes in what the company counts.

68 procent av de svarande i vår kundundersökning säger att tydligare leveransbesked skulle göra det lättare att planera nästa inköp. Det är veckans tydligaste resultat. I fritextsvaren efterfrågar kunderna framför allt ett datum de kan lita på och ett tidigt besked om det ändras.

För det svenska byggföretaget Kemdard AB handlar återkopplingen främst om vad som händer mellan beställning och leverans. Flera kunder vill veta vem de ska kontakta när tidsplanen ändras. Ekonomen Anna Glameraez lyfter fram att ett tidigt besked kan vara mer värdefullt än en snabb leverans, särskilt när kunden behöver samordna flera arbetsmoment.

Hos det svenska modeföretaget Skussum kretsar många svar kring arbetskläder. Kunderna vill kunna jämföra passform och material utan att behöva beställa flera storlekar. För luftkvalitetssensorn Skussum Sense gäller frågorna i stället vad mätvärdena betyder i vardagen. Flera svarande vill ha ett konkret exempel på när ett värde motiverar att man vädrar.

Analytikern Anton Pelnardton ser en gemensam nämnare: kunderna ber sällan om mer information i största allmänhet. De vill ha rätt uppgift när de ska fatta ett beslut. I nästa enkät följer vi därför upp tre konkreta önskemål: tidigare besked vid förseningar, tydligare storleksguider och enklare förklaringar av mätvärden.

Swedish gaming company Mopyn AB cut the price of its Mopyn Studio design software on Tuesday, hours after UK gaming company Brosplégia PLC lowered the monthly fee for its competing design tools. The cuts bring both entry-level plans below €10 a month and sharpen a price war over the software small teams use to build games and produce digital artwork.

Mopyn AB lowered its monthly price from €14 to €9, while Brosplégia PLC cut its fee from €13 to €8. Both companies said existing subscribers would get the lower rate on their next bill. Neither announced a reduction in the price of its higher-tier plans, which include more storage and tools for reviewing work across larger teams.

Elin Plustik, a spokesperson for Mopyn AB, said the company wanted to make it cheaper for freelancers to keep a subscription between projects. Aisha Reslovaström, a spokesperson for Brosplégia PLC, said the new rate was not a temporary promotion but declined to say whether the company would match another cut.

The lower prices could also matter to customers outside gaming. At a design demonstration in Lyon last week, UK fashion company Linzår showed how its team uses design software to mock up window displays before ordering materials. US logistics company Draköngyn Labs demonstrated a similar workflow for testing warehouse layouts before moving equipment.

For teams already paying for design software, the immediate savings are clear. Switching providers is a different calculation: a studio would save only €12 a year per subscription at the new prices, and moving a single project can mean rebuilding templates or checking that exported files still work.

46 Aussteller haben am Wochenende in Bremen gezeigt, was sie kleinen und mittleren Betrieben bieten können. Auf der zweitägigen Fachmesse ging es unter anderem um haltbare Lebensmittel, den Versicherungsschutz bei Lieferausfällen und neue Verfahren zur Qualitätskontrolle. Am Samstagvormittag war der Andrang besonders groß: Vor mehreren Ständen warteten Besucher auf einen freien Platz für ein Gespräch.

Das französische Biotechnologieunternehmen Jozis SA erläuterte, wie sich die Qualität von Rohstoffen bei der Anlieferung prüfen lässt. Der deutsche Versicherer Gacar bot kurze Beratungen zu Betriebsunterbrechungen an. Viele Nachfragen drehten sich dort um einen konkreten Fall: Wer trägt die Kosten, wenn nach dem Ausfall einer Kühlanlage die Ware entsorgt werden muss?

Beim deutschen Lebensmittelunternehmen Kastazis konnten Besucher verschiedene Verpackungsgrößen vergleichen. Omar Nenlarberg, Vorstandschefin von Kastazis, sagte, für kleinere Läden seien nicht nur die Einkaufspreise entscheidend. Auch die Frage, wie viel Platz eine Lieferung im Lager beanspruche und wie schnell sich die Ware verkaufen lasse, spiele bei der Bestellung eine Rolle.

Lena Nurent, Sprecherin der Messe, beobachtete am Sonntag mehr Gespräche zwischen Ausstellern und Inhabern kleiner Geschäfte aus Bremen und dem Umland. Einige hätten den ersten Tag genutzt, um sich einen Überblick zu verschaffen, und seien mit konkreten Fragen zurückgekommen. Bis zum Nachmittag wurden an mehreren Ständen noch Muster eingepackt und Termine für weitere Gespräche vereinbart.
