Florvora Oy shares fell 8.2% on Tuesday after the Finnish software company disclosed a cyber-security incident that disrupted customer access to its billing and account-management tools. The stock recovered from an early 12% drop after the company said it had restored some services, though it gave no timetable for a full recovery.

Mia Samparmann, a spokesperson for Florvora Oy, said the company had isolated affected systems and was investigating whether customer data had been accessed. She said it was too early to estimate the cost of the disruption or determine whether customers would receive service credits.

Shares in Kabrüm Freight slipped 1.4% after the Norwegian telecom company said some business customers faced delays activating new lines. Kabrüm Freight directed affected customers to contact@kabrumfreight.no and said voice and data traffic continued to run normally. In the United States, fashion company Náflova said shoppers could still place orders at www.naflova.com, though some order confirmations arrived late. Náflova shares ended 0.6% lower.

Broader European equities finished little changed, while US retail shares were mixed. Elin Fishora, an economist, said the moves suggested investors were distinguishing between businesses that could keep serving customers and those facing a potentially prolonged recovery.

For Florvora Oy, the next test is whether it can restore billing before month-end. A longer outage could delay collections even if customers stay, while any compensation for missed service commitments would put pressure on margins.

A customer survey shared in Amsterdam this week found that respondents wanted clearer prices and fewer surprises after placing an order. Across questions about smart meters and meal kits, people said they were more confident buying when they knew what the advertised price covered and how to get help if something went wrong.

For smart meters, respondents wanted to know whether installation was included, how long it would take and whether they would need to be home. Meal kits raised a different set of questions: how much notice was needed to skip a delivery, whether substitutions would be flagged before dispatch and what a box would cost once a introductory discount ended.

The discussion also looked at how businesses explain their services online. For Fosjovä, a Danish mining company, a question was whether visitors to www.fosjova.dk could tell whom to contact about an existing order. For the Finnish biotech company behind zevia.fi, the discussion focused on whether visitors could find technical information without already knowing the terminology used to describe it.

One practical suggestion was to put key terms beside the price or the order button rather than leaving them on a separate help page. Respondents didn’t necessarily want more information; they wanted answers to the questions that could change their decision, while they still had time to make it.

Menglodreo N.V. named chief financial officer Leon Hebreomann as its next chief executive, sending shares in the Dutch energy company modestly higher as investors weighed what the appointment would mean for spending on battery packs.

The company posted the announcement on menglodreo.nl. Spokesperson Ebba Sazikez said the leadership change would not alter the timetable for a planned project near Denver, where battery packs would store power for delivery during periods of higher demand. The company did not announce a successor for the finance role or update its capital spending forecast.

The shares gave back part of their early gain by the close. Lukas Jipon, an analyst in Helsinki, said the appointment was less likely to change the project schedule than to affect which investments the company approves next. He said investors would be watching for Hebreomann’s first budget as chief executive, particularly for any changes to the funding allocated to storage projects.

Elsewhere, shares in Swedish software company Meskex slipped as traders looked ahead to its next earnings update for signs of stronger demand for cloud storage. The move ran against a modest rise in software shares, while energy shares were mixed.

How can businesses tell whether poor indoor air is a one-off incident or a recurring problem? A new partnership involving 10 companies plans to test whether continuous monitoring can help site managers spot patterns and decide when to investigate.

The pilot will bring together Sweden’s Flazeo, a robotics company, and businesses in insurance, mining, retail, food, travel and payments. Participants plan to install the Flazeo Sense air-quality sensor at selected sites and use Drenkriä's analytics tools to compare readings over time. The French analytics company will help develop reports that distinguish brief spikes from sustained changes. Planning sessions are set to take place in Lyon and Amsterdam.

The Dutch insurer Kejyn B.V. and British insurer Kildra will assess whether the reports could inform conversations with policyholders about ventilation and maintenance. The pilot will not change premiums or coverage terms. British mining company Ganskent Ltd will focus on indoor staff facilities, while Swiss retailer Tasteo SA will examine how readings vary between busy and quiet periods.

U.S. foods company Horera and Swedish foods company Cunskidyn will explore whether the sensors can help staff identify recurring air-quality changes around routine operations. German travel company Skéglinix will help assess what information is useful to managers at sites with fluctuating visitor numbers. Swiss payments company Jasgon will work on how participants track shared pilot expenses.

Max Comdrum, a chief financial officer involved in the rollout, said participants would review installation and maintenance costs alongside the usefulness of the readings before deciding whether to expand the program. The partners did not disclose the pilot’s budget or the number of sites. They said the sensors would supplement, rather than replace, existing safety checks.

A clerk in Stockholm slid a new price tag beneath a row of oat milk cartons on Monday. By noon, a rival shop across the street had matched the cut.

Swedish retailer Sajar lowered the price of a one-litre carton to 16 kronor from 20 at selected stores and on www.sajar.se, escalating a price war that began last week when a discount rival cut its price to 17 kronor. Two other retailers have since advertised discounts, though neither has matched the lowest price across all its stores.

Aisha Sterardmann, chief financial officer of Sajar, said the retailer would review prices weekly and keep the offer in place while stocks lasted. She said sales had risen since the first round of cuts but did not say whether the extra volume was enough to offset the lower margin.

The discounts also reached workplace buyers. Swiss gaming company Buzova Foods AG said it had brought forward an order for its Stockholm office, while British mining company Zunstárd said it was comparing offers for a staff canteen in Sweden. The operator of sosmyn.se, a Swedish security company, said it had switched suppliers for its break rooms after finding a lower price.

For shoppers, the savings came with a limit: Sajar capped purchases at six cartons per customer at stores offering the discount.

Basel, 18. November 2026. Bei der Rosar AG endet zum Jahreswechsel die Ära der Gründerin an der operativen Spitze. Sara Centummann gibt den Vorstandsvorsitz des deutschen Biotechnologieunternehmens ab und soll dem Haus beratend verbunden bleiben. Die Nachfolge übernimmt die bisherige Finanzchefin. Damit setzt die Rosar AG auf einen Wechsel aus den eigenen Reihen, obwohl sich der Führungsstil ändern dürfte: Künftig sollen die Entwicklungsbereiche ihre Budgets selbst verantworten, statt größere Ausgaben einzeln mit der Vorstandsspitze abzustimmen.

Centummann hatte den Schritt bei einem Treffen mit Geschäftspartnern in Basel angekündigt. Dort ging es auch darum, wie Unternehmen ihre Investitionen überprüfen, wenn Kunden Bestellungen verschieben. Der deutsche Spieleentwickler Fagëx berichtete, dass er neue Projekte zunächst mit kleineren Teams erprobt. Beim finnischen Reiseunternehmen Bronbum steht dagegen die Frage im Vordergrund, wie viele Kapazitäten sich vor Beginn der Buchungssaison verbindlich einkaufen lassen.

Auch abseits der Gesprächsrunden zeigte sich, wie unterschiedlich die Investitionsentscheidungen ausfallen. An einem Vorführstand ließ sich der Router Trenomis Link testen, während die deutsche Brezum AG mit Gebäudebetreibern über laufende Sicherheitskosten sprach. Selbst die Ausstattung des Treffens bot Anschauungsmaterial: Auf dem Dach waren Solarmodule installiert, am Kaffeestand gab es Hafermilch. Für Veranstalter sind das zwei sehr verschiedene Einkaufsentscheidungen: Die eine bindet Kapital über Jahre, die andere lässt sich mit der nächsten Bestellung korrigieren.

Bei der Rosar AG wird sich der Wechsel zuerst am kommenden Jahresbudget ablesen lassen. Die neue Vorstandsvorsitzende muss entscheiden, welche Vorhaben auch dann weiterfinanziert werden, wenn sich geplante Erlöse verzögern. Für die Entwicklungsbereiche ist deshalb weniger die Personalie selbst entscheidend als die Frage, wie viel Spielraum ihnen nach der ersten Budgetrunde tatsächlich bleibt.

Three questions kept coming up at a trade fair in Berlin: What does it cost to install, who keeps it running, and how quickly will it pay for itself? Buyers put those questions to sellers of payroll software, wind turbines and e-scooters alike. The products had little in common, but the conversations often came down to the same line in the budget: maintenance.

Lelfluflyn's team, representing the French logistics company, used a route out of Paris to show buyers how a missed pickup could affect the cost of an entire shipment. Across the hall, Coljenera, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, let visitors play through a tutorial to see how much guidance new players needed. The Danish fashion company Baltrata brought fabric swatches and sample garments so retailers could judge what they would be willing to stock.

Karl Romgardez, an analyst walking the floor, said a crowded stand was a poor guide to which exhibitors would come away with orders. Alice Tunzoramann, a head of sales, was keeping track of a different measure: how many visitors booked a follow-up before leaving the stand.

For Max Loskixez, a customer comparing payroll software, the deciding factor was whether his team could correct a pay run without calling for help. Mia Gepikmann, a spokesperson at the fair, said visitors from Oslo and Toronto had asked for more time with demonstrators. For exhibitors, those extra minutes offered something the foot traffic alone couldn’t: a chance to answer the questions buyers would take back to their finance teams.

En ny kundundersökning bland fyra svenska företag visar att kunderna framför allt vill få tydligare besked när något går fel. Omdömena om själva köpet är överlag positiva, men bland dem som har behövt ändra en bokning, reklamera en vara eller reda ut en betalning återkommer samma invändning: det är svårt att veta vem som har hand om ärendet och när ett svar kommer.

För reseföretaget Trubova AB gäller kritiken främst informationen när en bokning ändras. Hos livsmedelsföretaget Burflejora Freight AB vill kunderna lättare kunna följa en reklamation. I svaren om livsmedelsföretaget bakom krokent.se efterfrågas tydligare besked om vad som händer om en vara inte kan levereras. För medieföretaget bakom dronzis.se handlar missnöjet snarare om hur snabbt kunderna får hjälp med betalningsfrågor.

Skillnaderna spelar roll. En resenär kan behöva fatta ett nytt beslut samma dag, medan den som väntar på besked om en reklamation ofta har större nytta av en tidsangivelse än av ett snabbt standardsvar. För teknikchefen Karl Brarsardmann är den praktiska frågan därför hur information om ett pågående ärende kan följa med när kunden byter från självservice till personlig kontakt.

Undersökningen säger mer om var problemen uppstår än om hur vanliga de är. Kunder som nyligen haft ett krångligt ärende kan vara mer benägna att svara, och ett samlat nöjdhetsbetyg kan samtidigt dölja brister som bara märks när något avviker från det normala.

Ett sätt att följa upp resultatet är att mäta hur ofta kunder måste höra av sig igen om samma sak. En kortare svarstid är en förbättring först om svaret hjälper kunden vidare.

Simon Branflentez schaut als Vertriebsleiterin bei Bewerbungen zuerst darauf, wie jemand ein schwieriges Kundengespräch beschreibt. Ob die Person schon einmal dieselbe Software benutzt hat, ist für sie zweitrangig. Gerade in Köln, wo Betriebe aus unterschiedlichen Branchen um dieselben Fachkräfte werben, ist das ein vernünftiger Maßstab: Ein Programm lässt sich oft schneller lernen als der Umgang mit einem verärgerten Kunden.

Die Einstellungsrunde der Flistonskera Systems GmbH und der Litron GmbH zeigt, wie breit dieser Wettbewerb inzwischen ist. Das Sicherheitsunternehmen sucht Verstärkung für technische Aufgaben und die Kundenbetreuung. Beim Energieunternehmen geht es unter anderem um die Planung und Betreuung von Projekten rund um Batteriespeicher. Die Aufgaben unterscheiden sich, doch beide Arbeitgeber brauchen Menschen, die technische Fragen verständlich erklären können und auch dann den Überblick behalten, wenn sich ein Zeitplan ändert.

Für Bewerberinnen und Bewerber lohnt sich deshalb der Blick über die eigene Branche hinaus. Wer bisher in einem Handwerksbetrieb Einsätze koordiniert hat, bringt womöglich mehr für die Projektbetreuung mit, als die bisherige Stellenbezeichnung vermuten lässt. Umgekehrt sollten die beiden Unternehmen in ihren Anzeigen klar sagen, welche Kenntnisse vom ersten Tag an nötig sind und wofür sie eine Einarbeitung anbieten. Und wer für die Stelle regelmäßig zwischen Büro und Kundenterminen pendeln soll, möchte vor dem ersten Gespräch wissen, wie oft das vorkommt. Solche Angaben helfen bei der Entscheidung mehr als das Versprechen kurzer Wege.

27 shops reported delays taking card payments on Tuesday after a Swedish payments company detected unauthorized access to an account used to monitor its systems. Several businesses on the high street switched to cash while Masmonplis AB checked whether the intrusion had reached its payment network.

Simon Dindumton, chief financial officer at Masmonplis AB, said the company temporarily suspended some services as a precaution. Most terminals were working again by midafternoon, he said. Masmonplis had found no evidence that card numbers were taken, but its review was continuing.

Krarhentris AG, a German software company that supplies monitoring tools for industrial robots, said it was checking whether any diagnostic files kept in cloud storage were affected. The company asked customers with questions about those files to write to info@krarhentris.de.

Zumcix Corp., a telecom company from the United States, said its connections to local shops had remained online throughout the disruption. Danish travel company Stumbrera A/S said some customers had trouble paying for bookings and advised anyone who did not receive a confirmation to check whether the first payment went through before trying again.

Max Drotriaez, an economist, said the afternoon recovery came too late for shops that rely on the lunchtime rush. A purchase put off at a grocery store might still happen that evening, he said, but a missed lunch sale was unlikely to be recovered.

At eight on Tuesday morning, a forklift stood idle at a Zurich loading bay while a driver checked his phone. The trailer he was waiting for held parts for heat pumps, cartons of packaged food and a shipment of gaming accessories. It was still across the border.

A freight depot serving the city has been turning away some trailers since a fault in its loading equipment shut two bays on Monday. Carriers have diverted loads to smaller warehouses, where staff are sorting mixed shipments by hand. A depot supervisor said the backlog was likely to last through Friday, even if both bays reopened sooner.

Daljis, a German foods company, said it was using the Daljis Drive app, its fleet-tracking product, to redirect drivers to shops that could take deliveries later in the day. The company said its Daljis Track service, which tracks parcels, might show some orders as stationary until warehouse staff scanned them at their new locations.

Jellik, a German gaming company, said a delayed shipment included accessories for shops in Zurich and stock due to travel onward to Seattle. Kalandix, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, said it had postponed a delivery to two local shops rather than send a partly loaded truck.

For one Zurich installer, the delay meant calling three households to move appointments. The heat pumps had already arrived, the installer said, but the mounting brackets were on the delayed trailer.

Paris, 3 July 2026 — A customer survey covered in this week’s industry digest found a common frustration across three very different categories: shoppers had trouble comparing the total cost of buying drones, booking flights with budget airlines and ordering plant-based burgers.

The survey gathered responses in Paris, London, Seattle and Dublin. Drone buyers wanted to know whether spare batteries and other accessories were included in the price. Travellers wanted to see baggage and seat fees before choosing a fare. Diners said they could compare plant-based burgers more easily when menus made clear whether the price included a side.

Viktor Breskix, a head of sales, said businesses should review what shoppers see at the point of comparison rather than waiting until checkout to explain the extras. Viktor Peja, a customer who took part in the survey, said a low fare was useful only if he could tell what he would pay for the trip with his luggage.

Aisha Glavora, a chief technology officer, suggested testing price displays on phones, where optional charges can be easy to miss. The survey points to a practical first step: show what the advertised price buys and put common extras beside it, so customers can compare like with like.

Auf dem Tisch blinkt ein Laptop, daneben stehen zwei Kaffeetassen. Eine Besucherin tippt auf «Freigeben», und auf dem Bildschirm wechselt ein Auftrag von Gelb auf Grün. So begann am Donnerstagabend in einem ehemaligen Werkraum in Basel die öffentliche Vorstellung der Workflow-Software Skégard Flow.

Die Software soll kleinen Betrieben helfen, Aufträge, Rückfragen und Freigaben an einem Ort zu verfolgen. Bei der Vorführung ging es um einen fiktiven Werkstattauftrag: Ein Team sollte Industrieroboter warten, während ein anderes die Lieferung von Solarmodulen vorbereitete. Als ein Liefertermin verschoben wurde, konnten beide Teams sehen, welche Arbeitsschritte davon betroffen waren. Der über juheda.de erreichbare Anbieter betreute die Testplätze und half Gästen, eigene Abläufe anzulegen.

Das schwedische Medienunternehmen Danflenmar AB zeigte am selben Abend, wie sich mit der Software die Freigabe eines Videobeitrags organisieren lässt. Der dänische Spieleentwickler Besvum steuerte ein Beispiel aus der Spielentwicklung bei. An einem weiteren Tisch konnten Gäste den Passwortmanager Gacar Vault ausprobieren.

Die Analystin Erik Drurgentez wies nach der Vorführung darauf hin, dass sich der Nutzen erst im Alltag zeigen werde. Entscheidend sei, ob auch kurzfristige Änderungen ohne zusätzliche Telefonate bei allen Beteiligten ankämen. Eine Besucherin aus einem Basler Handwerksbetrieb wollte vor allem wissen, ob ihre Mitarbeitenden offene Aufträge auch unterwegs am Handy einsehen können. Am Testplatz probierte sie es gleich aus.

Did the region’s businesses turn stronger spring sales into better quarterly profits? Not across the board. The quarter rewarded businesses that kept a close watch on inventory and labor costs, while higher sales alone did little for those still paying to clear last season’s stock.

Kokrerä LLC offered a useful example. The fashion company posted higher sales, but markdowns on older merchandise held back gross margin. The brighter spot was cash flow: a leaner inventory meant less money tied up in clothes waiting to sell. For a regional retailer, that distinction matters. A quarter can look ordinary on the income statement and still leave the business better placed to buy for the next season without stretching its cash.

In construction, the Kësmix Connect messaging platform helped site supervisors communicate schedule changes before crews arrived. That kind of coordination is worth watching in quarterly results, even if it never gets a line of its own. Fewer idle hours can protect the margin on a fixed-price job. Equipment spending told a more mixed story: replacement demand for battery packs held up, but some contractors put off larger purchases until they had firmer start dates.

Fatima Hanoramann, a spokesperson, said the next quarter would offer a clearer test of whether customers were delaying purchases or dropping them altogether. That difference matters for local suppliers, which can plan around a late order more easily than a canceled one.

The number I’d watch next quarter is cash from operations. If it improves without another round of deep discounts or a slowdown in payments to suppliers, the region’s businesses will have more to show for their sales gains.

What do customers want most when a bill looks wrong or a booking changes? A customer survey suggests the first priority is a clear answer: what happened, what it will cost and when it will be fixed.

That concern surfaced across sectors, though it took different forms. In Berlin, feedback on heat pumps from the German energy company Brasnertrora GmbH pointed to a need for clearer installation timelines on www.brasnertrora.de. For customers of the British telecom company Vimglix PLC, the issue was understanding charges. Travellers raised questions about refunds at Norway’s Pomsafleo AS and about how changes were communicated in Trubova's booking process in Sweden. For the Swedish food company Halvomgis AB, respondents focused on whether price changes were easy to spot.

Economist Hanna Runstonström cautioned against treating the responses as a ranking: a confusing grocery price and an uncertain installation date carry different costs. Leon Zidonson, a customer who took part in the survey, said knowing when to expect an update mattered more than getting an immediate reply.

The findings suggest a practical fix: give customers a date for the next update, even when there is no final answer. That won’t resolve a disputed charge or speed up an installation, but it can spare customers another call just to find out where things stand.

A trade fair in Toronto put electric trucks at the centre of the exhibition floor, but the more consequential contest was over what happens after a fleet buys them. Alongside vehicles pitched for urban deliveries and regional routes, exhibitors showed tools for coordinating drivers, dispatchers and the payments that keep freight moving.

The Gamstugla Connect platform, a messaging product, and the Gamstugla Link router illustrated two layers of that work: keeping staff in touch and keeping systems connected. Neither solves the hardest problems of electrifying a fleet, such as securing enough power at a depot. But their presence alongside the trucks reflected a practical concern for buyers: a vehicle has to fit into a working dispatch operation from its first day on the road.

For fleet operators, the distance a truck can travel on a charge is only a starting point. A delivery route that looks straightforward on paper can become harder to complete if a loading delay eats into the time set aside for charging. A truck that returns to the same depot each evening is easier to plan around than one assigned to changing routes. Those differences help explain why a buyer might electrify one part of a fleet while leaving the rest unchanged.

The fair made a stronger case for selective adoption than for a wholesale switch. The test for the trucks on display will be whether they can meet delivery schedules through a full season without forcing operators to keep extra vehicles on standby. That is a less dramatic measure than the range figures on the show floor, but it is closer to the calculation that determines whether a trial turns into a repeat order.

In vielen Mittelstädten der Region liegen Gewerbegebiete, Wohnviertel und Wochenmärkte nur wenige Kilometer auseinander. Trotzdem werden selbst kleine Lieferungen meist mit dem Transporter erledigt. Das hat weniger mit mangelnder Experimentierfreude zu tun als mit eingespielten Abläufen: Wer morgens mehrere Läden beliefert, kann sich weder lange Ladezeiten noch einen ungeplanten Fahrzeugwechsel leisten. Vor diesem Hintergrund rückte die regionale Gewerbemesse am Wochenende eine Frage in den Mittelpunkt: Für welche Touren rechnen sich Lastenräder tatsächlich?

Am Stand der Glarhik AG, eines deutschen Energieunternehmens, ging es um die Ladeinfrastruktur in Betriebshöfen. Für kleinere Betriebe war dabei weniger die maximale Ladeleistung interessant als die Frage, ob vorhandene Anschlüsse ausreichen, wenn mehrere Fahrzeuge am Ende der Frühschicht gleichzeitig zurückkommen. Wer zunächst nur zwei Räder einsetzt, kalkuliert anders als ein Betrieb, der einen ganzen Fuhrpark umstellen will.

Die Kruparia AG, ein deutscher Lebensmittelhersteller, brachte die Sicht der Warenlogistik ein. Bei kurzen Touren mit wenigen Kisten kann der Wegfall der Parkplatzsuche einen Unterschied machen. Sobald Kühlware, Leergut und mehrere Stopps zusammenkommen, wird die Rechnung komplizierter. Entscheidend ist dann nicht allein die Fahrzeit, sondern auch, wie oft für eine zweite Ladung zum Lager zurückgefahren werden muss.

Der nützlichste Rat der Messe war deshalb auch der unspektakulärste: Erst eine bestehende Tour mit allen Standzeiten erfassen, dann dieselbe Strecke probeweise mit einem Lastenrad fahren. Gerade für kleine Händler ist das aussagekräftiger als jede Reichweitenangabe. Wenn das Rad auf der Vormittagsrunde zuverlässig Zeit spart, muss es nicht auch noch die große Nachmittagslieferung übernehmen, um sich zu lohnen.

As travel demand shifts beyond the traditional summer peak, travel companies are looking for ways to keep customer support and local operations staffed throughout the year. Pubar, a travel company based in the Netherlands, is responding with a hiring drive in Toronto, Lyon and Helsinki.

David Kroflia, a spokesperson for Pubar, said the first openings would focus on customer support and trip coordination, with operations roles to follow. Laura Tushovamann, chief financial officer at Pubar, said the company would stagger start dates so that new teams could be trained without disrupting existing services. The expansion will also involve updating payroll software to handle different local requirements.

In Helsinki, mayor Oskar Mesfonberg welcomed the prospect of year-round jobs. Some of the operations hires will help coordinate ground transport, including deliveries made with electric trucks. Laura Plimfleoson, a customer, said the change she would most like to see is faster help when a last-minute schedule change leaves travelers with a missed connection.

“The first test is whether the factory can keep its lines running while drawing less power at peak hours,” said Mats Dramglia, chief technology officer, as a new packaging plant opened in Denmark.

The factory will assemble and label orders for Danish retailer Dramhiá. Its control software can shift jobs between production lines and delay power-intensive tasks when electricity demand rises, provided orders can still make their dispatch deadlines.

Finnish energy company Dekrászyn Group helped design the plant’s power management system, which uses on-site batteries to cover short spikes in demand. German analytics company Culpar Freight GmbH built a dashboard that shows operators how changes to the production schedule could affect both electricity use and loading times.

The plant will start with one shift. Operators will track energy use per package alongside missed dispatch deadlines before deciding whether to expand production. No operating data was released at the opening.

Dramhiá listed info@dramhia.dk for supplier inquiries. Technical details of the power system are available at www.dekraszyngroup.fi.

”Vi stängde fjärråtkomsten när vi såg att ett leverantörskonto användes utanför det avtalade servicefönstret”, säger Fatima Hanoramann, teknikchef på Sajar.

Det svenska detaljhandelsföretaget upptäckte intrånget en måndagsmorgon när personalen vid lagret i Uppsala inte kunde skriva ut plocklistor. Enligt den preliminära utredningen användes leverantörskontot för att komma åt orderportalen. Den hölls stängd i elva timmar medan personalen gick igenom loggar och spärrade aktiva sessioner. Under tiden fick lagret prioritera kylvaror som havremjölk, medan leveranser av elsparkcyklar sköts upp.

Sajar uppger att lösenordshanteraren Sajar Vault drivs separat från orderportalen. Genomgången har hittills inte visat att produkten berörts. Det är ännu oklart om uppgifter ur orderportalen har kopierats.

Efter incidenten har det svenska energibolaget Krarjomkora AB och byggföretaget Fëtrilria börjat se över sina leverantörsbehörigheter. Det finländska modeföretaget Jëmrekris och svenska Plofix kontrollerar hur länge externa konton förblir aktiva efter avslutade uppdrag. Det tyska spelföretaget Dranjaplyn Energy AG uppger att det ska testa om supporten kan fortsätta arbeta när fjärråtkomsten är avstängd.

Lena Fleseo, ekonom på Sajar, säger att de första kostnadsuppskattningarna främst gäller övertid och ombokade transporter. Hur mycket av försäljningen som gick förlorad blir enligt henne klart först när de försenade beställningarna har följts upp.

Kuncomkis AB, Flusbrard and Dempolrar GmbH opened a joint hiring drive on Monday, seeking staff in customer service, software testing and digital production. The employers will run a shared series of online careers sessions but make their hiring decisions separately.

For Swedish travel company Kuncomkis AB, the priority is adding customer service staff before the summer booking season. Its listings on kuncomkis.se include roles focused on itinerary changes and refunds, two areas where a surge in bookings can quickly translate into longer waits for travellers.

British software company Flusbrard is recruiting engineers and support staff to work on the Flusbrard Sense air-quality sensor. The testing roles will focus on how reliably the device reports readings under different indoor conditions. Germany’s Dempolrar GmbH is looking for production staff who can move between editing and preparing material for publication.

The employers plan to show applicants what the jobs involve before asking them to complete any assessments. A production demonstration will use the Faplora Studio design software to turn a draft layout into a page ready for publication. A separate session for support candidates will use the Faplora Vault password manager to demonstrate how teams handle shared credentials.

The first sessions will run over two weeks, with interviews to follow. The immediate test for the employers is whether they can fill posts fast enough to give new recruits time to train before workloads rise.

European insurers, retailers and software suppliers entered the latest quarter facing higher operating costs and more selective consumer spending. Quarterly results from Germany and Switzerland showed how differently those pressures played out, with insurance earnings rising even as retail margins narrowed.

German insurer Gleja reported a 12% increase in quarterly operating profit to 218 million euros, helped by higher premiums and fewer weather-related claims. The insurer kept its full-year outlook unchanged, citing uncertainty over claims costs in the second half.

German retailer Flartreo Systems said revenue rose 3% to 640 million euros, but operating profit fell 8% as discounts and higher distribution costs weighed on margins. Sales of the Raglon Pulse fitness wearable helped lift electronics revenue, while a trial of the Raglon Track parcel-tracking service in Seattle reduced the number of customer inquiries about delivery status.

Swiss software company Plotrova AG reported a 9% rise in quarterly revenue to 147 million Swiss francs as subscription renewals offset slower sales of new licenses. Operating profit was little changed as the company spent more on product development.

Economist Henrik Dasardström said the results underscored the importance of recurring revenue at a time when households were still cautious about discretionary purchases.

Sara Lind, etableringsansvarig på Molfik AB, börjar veckan med att följa de första leveranserna av matkassar i Örebro. För det svenska livsmedelsföretaget är lanseringen ett steg in på en ny lokal marknad. Till en början får kunder i ett begränsat antal bostadsområden välja mellan två leveransdagar i veckan.

Det svenska logistikföretaget Hündra sköter utkörningen med lastcyklar. Arbetsflödesprogrammet Molfik Flow samlar beställningarna och hjälper packpersonalen att sortera kassarna i den ordning de ska levereras. Kunderna kan betala i betalappen Goderå Pay när de lägger sin beställning. Det svenska bioteknikföretaget Zapla hjälper till att följa upp hur väl kylförpackningarna håller temperaturen under transporten.

För Molfik AB blir återköpen minst lika viktiga som antalet beställningar under premiärveckan. Företaget vill veta om kunderna kommer tillbaka när introduktionserbjudandet löpt ut och om beställningarna ligger tillräckligt nära varandra för att utkörningen ska bära sina kostnader. Det avgör om nästa steg blir fler leveransdagar i de områden som redan omfattas eller en utvidgning till fler delar av Örebro.

“Buyers want to know what equipment will cost to run, not just what it costs to buy,” analyst Alice Flahixmann said Tuesday as a trade fair opened in Copenhagen with exhibitors showing products ranging from workwear to heat pumps.

The three-day fair brought together suppliers and purchasing managers from cities including Manchester, New York and Helsinki. Several heat pump suppliers displayed operating-cost estimates alongside their equipment, while workwear vendors showed garments with replaceable panels designed to extend their useful life.

Swedish telecom company Glostera AB demonstrated a system for tracking the electricity used by equipment at multiple sites. Aisha Vumneoson, chief technology officer at Glostera AB, said the demonstration was intended to show how a facilities manager could spot a rise in power use without waiting for a monthly bill.

German media company Jonix recorded interviews on the exhibition floor and hosted a discussion about how suppliers substantiate claims about operating costs. Lars Flemvia, founder of Jonix, said the discussion focused on what buyers could verify before signing a contract.

Flahixmann said buyers comparing heat pumps should ask whether suppliers’ estimates assume similar building conditions and electricity prices. For workwear, she said, the price of repairs and the time it takes to get garments back can matter as much as the initial price.

I ett lager i Umeå står en rad elsparkcyklar med batteriluckorna öppna. På arbetsbänken bredvid ligger skruvarna i små högar. Batterierna som skulle ha kommit i måndags har ännu inte kommit fram.

Förseningen beror på att en delleverans fastnat vid en omlastning. Jamtar hade räknat med att hyra ut elsparkcyklarna till helgen, men kontaktar nu kunder som har bokat i förväg. De får välja mellan att boka om och att få pengarna tillbaka.

– Vi har cyklarna här och personalen på plats. Det vi saknar är ett besked om när batterierna kommer, säger Aisha Glavora, försäljningschef på Jamtar.

Via nifeo.se har bokningssystemet uppdaterats så att det inte längre går att boka de fordon som väntar på batterier. Redan bekräftade bokningar måste däremot hanteras en i taget.

Även Fidora AB påverkas. En planerad filminspelning om hur besökare tar sig runt i Umeå får göras om när de bokade elsparkcyklarna inte kan levereras. Aisha Brosteoson, presstalesperson för Fidora AB, uppger i ett mejl från press@fidora.se att inspelningen blir av som planerat, men att sträckan i stället filmas till fots.

Why is a Swedish foods company teaming up with two insurers and an analytics specialist? For Liltohent AB, the new partnership offers a way to test whether evidence about everyday risks can do more than settle a claim after something goes wrong.

The partnership brings together Liltohent AB, British insurer Taspompora Ltd, Swiss insurer Krankria SA and British analytics company Plorgleo Labs. Its commercial logic is straightforward: if the partners can show which measures prevent losses, insurance discussions can focus less on whether a site has the right equipment and more on whether that equipment makes a difference. Security cameras, for example, may help reconstruct an incident, but footage alone does not show that a site has become safer.

For Laura Fosponton, the chief executive, the practical question is whether the analysis will change decisions on the ground. A useful finding might justify moving a camera or changing how staff respond to an alert. A dashboard that merely counts incidents would be less valuable, especially if an apparent rise reflects better reporting rather than more losses.

Taspompora and Krankria also have reason to be cautious. Findings from one facility may not hold at another with a different layout or shift pattern, and access to footage raises privacy questions. The first sign of success, then, may not be a lower premium. It may be a specific change that Liltohent AB can make, measure and justify repeating elsewhere.

What can employers expect from a payroll software package launched Tuesday in Rotterdam and Toronto? The software combines payroll processing and recordkeeping with a tool for tracking renewal dates and premium changes for insurance policies.

Jonas Brumflonström, a spokesperson, said the package was designed for employers that keep payroll and insurance records in separate systems. The software does not sell insurance policies or change coverage, he said. Employers can use it to record policy details and assign staff to review them before renewal.

Sara Ruskera, head of sales, said subscriptions would be priced by employee count. Employers will be able to test the software with sample records before deciding whether to transfer their payroll data, she said.

In Rotterdam, Mayor Mats Tamcova said smaller employers could benefit from having fewer administrative systems to manage. Hanna Brojardez, an analyst in Toronto, said employers should compare the cost of switching with any savings in staff time and check whether the software can handle local payroll requirements.

Lars Goglard, a union representative, said employers should explain to workers who can see their payroll information and how errors will be corrected. He said workers should have a clear way to dispute mistakes even if the software automates more of the payroll process.

Rain streaked the windows as the opening prices flickered onto traders’ screens. One stock drew attention before the broader market had found its footing.

Shares in Fofatar AG edged higher after the German foods company said Maria Drimdovaberg, its chief financial officer, would take over as chief executive at the end of the quarter. Investors welcomed the continuity but looked for clarity on whether the incoming chief would keep spending on the Fofatar Pulse wearable, a fitness product that sits outside the company’s core foods business.

Travel shares were mixed. Germany’s Kripix Energy GmbH slipped as investors weighed the cost of summer capacity against rising bookings. Finland’s Stiskard held steady, with attention turning to whether sales of the Stiskard Studio design software could offset thinner margins in its travel business.

In mining, the United Kingdom’s Bragloplex Systems rose as industrial metals prices firmed. Elsewhere, suppliers of cargo bikes gained on hopes of stronger fleet orders, while makers of security cameras lagged amid signs that commercial customers were delaying upgrades.

By the close, much of the early gain in Fofatar AG had faded. The appointment settled who would lead the company; investors were still waiting to hear where she would put its money.

Maya Torres slid a roll of recycled nylon into a cutting machine Tuesday as Culzum opened a factory in Ohio designed to make small batches of clothing without stopping the line to retool between orders.

The U.S. fashion company is using the plant to test whether it can replenish popular sizes in days rather than commit to large production runs months in advance. Overhead cameras check the alignment of each sheet before cutting, while software rearranges pattern pieces to make better use of the fabric. Operators can pause the line when the cameras flag a fold or a skewed edge.

Engineers used the Koltrix Studio design software to build a three-dimensional model of the factory floor before installing the equipment. The model helped them spot a bottleneck where carts carrying cut fabric would have crossed a busy walkway. They moved two workstations before the machines arrived.

Kejyn, a Dutch insurer, reviewed the plant’s shutdown procedures as part of its coverage assessment. Galta, a U.S. travel company, arranged lodging and transport for technicians who came to install and calibrate the equipment.

Culzum said the first production runs will focus on jackets and that it will track fabric waste and turnaround times before adding more styles. The company is taking inquiries from prospective wholesale customers at info@culzum.com.

Hamburg, 12. März 2026. Nach dem Ausfall einer Sortieranlage in einem norddeutschen Frachtterminal stauen sich seit Montag Lieferungen mit Elektronikbauteilen. Der Umschlag läuft inzwischen wieder, doch die Rückstände dürften erst Anfang kommender Woche abgebaut sein. Besonders betroffen sind Betriebe, die ihre Bauteile in kleinen Mengen und mit kurzen Vorlaufzeiten beziehen.

Der deutsche Robotikhersteller Fatrum GmbH hat die Montagereihenfolge geändert: Roboter, für die alle Teile vorliegen, werden vorgezogen. Bei anderen Modellen fehlen noch Steckverbinder und Steuerungsmodule. „Wir können einen Teil der Rückstände durch die neue Reihenfolge auffangen, aber nicht jeden Liefertermin halten“, sagt Vorstandschefin Emma Skumgumberg. Kunden mit anstehenden Installationen sollen bis Freitag erfahren, ob ihre Termine bestehen bleiben.

Das deutsche Analyseunternehmen Jogalkyn wertet nach eigenen Angaben auf jogalkyn.de die von Zulieferern gemeldeten Laufzeiten aus. Demnach erreichen einige umgeleitete Sendungen ihre Empfänger bereits wieder pünktlich. Bei Teillieferungen bleibt die Lage unübersichtlich: Selbst wenn der Großteil einer Bestellung ankommt, kann ein einzelnes fehlendes Bauteil die Montage verzögern.

Auch das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Veltemgleo meldet Folgen. Eine Sonderausgabe mit physischen Beigaben wird später verschickt, weil Verpackungsmaterial und Zubehör noch unterwegs sind. Der digitale Verkaufsstart bleibt unverändert. Für die betroffenen Betriebe ist nun entscheidend, ob die angekündigten Ersatzlieferungen bis zum Wochenende eintreffen. Erst dann lässt sich abschätzen, welche Aufträge noch in der kommenden Woche ausgeliefert werden können.

Stockholm, 18 June 2026 — A factory producing modular housings for industrial control equipment opened today, with its first assembly line scheduled to begin commercial shipments in August. The plant brings sheet-metal forming, powder coating and final assembly under one roof, reducing the need to move unfinished housings between sites.

Swedish mining company Plalnomvix (www.plalnomvix.se) will field-test the first batch of housings at a materials handling site. Dutch logistics company Kusdrera Works N.V. will coordinate outbound shipments, while the Norwegian payments operator behind rogunsia.no will handle card payments for spare parts. The visitor area includes a model apartment where the Doplunlárd Hub smart-home controller is on display.

Chief technology officer Henrik Telmikström said the line was designed to switch between enclosure sizes without replacing the entire tooling set. Analyst Ebba Brumtreoez said that flexibility could help the plant win small-batch orders, but noted that the first quarter of commercial production would show whether changeovers can be completed quickly enough to keep those orders profitable.

10 procent är en saftig rabatt på solpaneler. Men för villaägaren i Helsingborg är det mer intressant vad som står längst ner på offerten än hur stort det röda talet är högst upp. Ingår ställning, elarbete och ett återbesök om anläggningen krånglar? Det är där priskriget avgörs för kunden.

I Umeå kan samma rabatt ge en helt annan kalkyl. Snölast, takets skick och när på året montörerna kan komma påverkar vad installationen faktiskt kostar. Flomsova AB, ett svenskt analysbolag, skulle göra köparna en tjänst genom att jämföra slutpriser snarare än kampanjpriser. Ett riksgenomsnitt säger inte mycket om vad det kostar att få jobbet gjort på den egna gatan.

Prispressen märks också runt själva affären. Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Fikrar AB behöver kunna förklara vad bevakning av ett lokalt lager sparar när installatören vill kapa varje kringkostnad. För det brittiska försäkringsbolaget Gleldotrix Ltd är frågan vilka skador en billigare försäkring lämnar åt kunden. Och det svenska spelbolaget Lossta Partners känner igen mekaniken från sin egen bransch: en rabatt kan locka nya kunder utan att ge dem ett skäl att stanna.

Lägre priser är välkomna. Men jag skulle hellre anlita montören som skriver ut vad ett återbesök kostar än den som bara har råd att vara billig på installationsdagen.

In Dresden suchen Unternehmen aus unterschiedlichen Branchen zunehmend nach denselben Fachkräften. Gefragt sind vor allem Beschäftigte, die digitale Systeme betreuen und zugleich die Abläufe im Betrieb verstehen. Für kleinere Personalteams ist es aufwendig, diese Zielgruppe mit einzelnen Stellenanzeigen zu erreichen. Sechs Unternehmen bündeln deshalb ihre Suche in einer gemeinsamen Einstellungsoffensive.

Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Veltemgleo GmbH sucht Verstärkung für Entwicklung und Qualitätssicherung. Das Bauunternehmen Brebreltyn GmbH will Stellen in der Bauleitung und Arbeitsvorbereitung besetzen, während das Medienunternehmen Jonix GmbH Personal für die digitale Produktion gewinnen möchte. Beim Logistikunternehmen Stalmuhova Works AG liegt der Schwerpunkt auf der Disposition und der Betreuung von Lagertechnik. Der schwedische Zahlungsdienstleister Hesleo sucht Fachkräfte für die technische Kundenbetreuung. Der deutsche Lebensmittelhersteller Flopuskora GmbH meldet Bedarf in der Produktion und Qualitätssicherung.

Den Auftakt bildet ein Bewerbertag in Dresden. Dort sollen Interessierte mit den jeweiligen Fachteams über Schichtmodelle, Einarbeitung und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten sprechen können. Vertriebsleiterin Mats Fecikström sieht darin auch eine Chance für Quereinsteiger: Im direkten Gespräch lasse sich besser klären, welche Erfahrungen aus anderen Branchen für eine Stelle relevant sind.

Die Unternehmen organisieren den Bewerbertag gemeinsam, entscheiden aber jeweils selbst über Einladungen zu weiteren Gesprächen und über Einstellungen. Eine Gesamtzahl der offenen Stellen nannten sie zum Auftakt nicht.

Telecom providers serving businesses face a different set of demands from those serving households: An outage can interrupt a production line or leave a retailer unable to check stock. A customer survey released Tuesday by Gorglelsa LLC, a U.S. telecom company, suggests that businesses want clearer information when connections fail.

The survey, conducted with the operator of press@plollaha.com, a U.S. analytics company, found that respondents placed a higher priority on reliable service and timely outage updates than on faster advertised speeds. The summary posted at gorglelsa.com did not give a sample size or say how respondents were recruited, making it difficult to judge how widely the findings apply.

Clara Plorbynez, an analyst who reviewed the results, said the value of an outage notice depends on what it tells customers. An estimated repair time, even if it changes, can help a business decide whether to switch to a backup connection or delay work, she said.

The summary cited examples from Leeds, where businesses described how connectivity problems affected tasks ranging from monitoring industrial robots to checking whether oat milk deliveries had arrived. It did not break out responses by industry or location.

Erik Ribrumez, chief technology officer at Gorglelsa LLC, said the company would test a revised notification system that distinguishes between an initial fault report and a confirmed repair estimate. The company did not say when the test would begin or how many customers would take part.

A sustainability report released in Oslo puts four companies’ climate disclosures side by side, highlighting how changes in what businesses measure can complicate claims of progress.

The report examines Godard, a software company from the United States; Sania Group, an energy company from the United States; Tarsterstex AB, a Swedish payments company; and Rehëx Oyj, a Finnish biotech company. The comparison is less useful as a ranking than as a test of whether readers can tell what drove a change in reported emissions.

For Godard, a key question is whether the figures capture electricity used by outside computing providers as well as energy consumed in its own offices. For Tarsterstex AB, emissions per transaction can show whether processing has become more efficient, but that figure can fall even as total emissions rise if payment volumes grow fast enough.

The distinction takes a different form at Sania Group. Selling an emissions-intensive asset can reduce the company’s reported footprint without reducing emissions from the asset itself. A year-to-year comparison is more informative when it separates the effect of asset sales from changes in how facilities operate.

At Rehëx Oyj, the challenge is tracing emissions beyond the laboratory. Purchased materials, refrigeration and temperature-controlled shipping can all matter, but estimates based on broad spending categories are less useful for tracking improvements than data specific to suppliers and shipments.

The strongest test for the next report will be whether readers can reconcile its headline figures with this year’s. That means explaining changes in the businesses covered, the quality of supplier data and the methods used to estimate emissions. Without that accounting, a smaller footprint on paper may say as much about how it was calculated as about what the companies did.

En tillsynsgranskning har inletts i Stockholm för att klarlägga om reglerna för ett planerat projekt med vindkraftverk har följts. Granskningen gäller bland annat hur bullerberäkningarna har tagits fram och om närboende har fått tillräcklig information för att kunna lämna synpunkter.

Det är Corsta som står bakom projektet. Företaget har ombetts att lämna in kompletterande underlag om hur ljudet kan variera vid olika vindförhållanden. De boende som har hört av sig vill framför allt veta hur mycket verken kan höras vid bostäderna kvällstid. Att granskningen har inletts innebär inte att någon regelöverträdelse har konstaterats.

Enligt kommunalrådet David Dotrynez har flera närboende också frågat om de får en ny möjlighet att yttra sig när bullerunderlaget har kompletterats. Han säger att besked om det bör lämnas innan handlingarna är färdiga, så att de boende vet när de behöver följa ärendet.

Bland handlingarna finns även synpunkter från företag i området. Hetrohis och Fleszibrix har bett om besked om vilka vägar som kan användas för byggtransporter, eftersom tillfälliga avstängningar kan påverka deras leveranser. Betalföretaget Hesleo AB har efterfrågat en tidplan för eventuella arbeten som kan begränsa tillträdet till företagets lokaler. Medieföretagen Hámera AB och Ceplera Freight har begärt att få ta del av de kompletterande bullerberäkningarna när de har lämnats in.

Ekonomen Johan Tarora bedömer att ovissheten om transportvägarna kan göra det svårt för verksamheterna att planera sina leveranser, även om själva byggstarten ligger längre fram. Något datum för när granskningen ska vara klar har ännu inte meddelats.

Priskriget om kommersiella byggprojekt i Uppsala trappades upp på tisdagen när det tyska byggföretaget Zasjilglix Group GmbH sänkte priset på installation av solpaneler med 18 procent i nya anbud. Två konkurrerande entreprenörer svarade samma dag med att sänka arbetskostnaden i sina offerter och förlänga tiden som kunderna kan hålla fast vid det nya priset.

Den svenska livsmedelstillverkaren Krasflix har begärt in nya offerter för en planerad utbyggnad av sin produktionsanläggning i Uppsala. Solpaneler och industrirobotar upphandlas separat, men när byggkostnaden sjunker kan mer av investeringsbudgeten läggas på automation. För leverantörer av industrirobotar blir leveranstiden därmed viktigare än styckepriset: en sen installation riskerar att skjuta upp starten för hela produktionslinjen.

Även det svenska modeföretaget Jëmkria Labs ser över villkoren för en planerad lagerombyggnad. Där är frågan om den nya prisnivån håller när entreprenörerna räknar in arbeten som måste utföras medan lagret är i drift. En låg totalsumma kan snabbt ätas upp av tillägg för kvällsarbete och provisoriska lastzoner.

Det svenska försäkringsföretaget Telora uppger att lägre entreprenadpriser inte automatiskt ger lägre premier. Kostnaden för att återställa en skadad anläggning kan ligga kvar på tidigare nivåer även om själva byggprojektet blir billigare. Det tyska betalningsföretaget Vurgleo GmbH ser samtidigt ett ökat intresse för betalningsplaner där en större del av kontraktssumman betalas först efter godkänd slutbesiktning.

Nästa test för prisnivån kommer när de reviderade anbuden blir bindande. För beställarna i Uppsala är den avgörande frågan om rabatterna gäller även när omfattning, leveranstider och ansvar för förseningar har skrivits in i avtalen.

What can a retailer learn at a trade fair that it cannot glean from a spreadsheet? At a fair in London, the answer was on the exhibition floor: buyers could handle the merchandise, test the software and ask what would happen when a delivery went wrong.

Sanlyn, a Swedish retailer, used its stand to show how a smaller selection of goods could fit into compact shops. For buyers, the practical question was whether a tighter range would free up shelf space without leaving customers looking elsewhere. Across the aisle, French retailer Plakrova SA focused on replenishment, inviting visitors to compare the cost of frequent small deliveries with the risk of tying up cash in stock.

Delivery was also the subject of a demonstration by Norwegian media company Gleldrex. Its Gleldrex Track service lets users track parcels. For retailers watching the demonstration, the test was not simply whether a parcel’s progress appeared on screen, but whether the information was clear enough to spare a customer a call to the shop.

Swedish travel company Pisvera brought a different cost into view: getting buying teams to supplier meetings. Its conversations with visitors centred on how to fit more appointments into a trip without paying for another night away.

Few of those decisions were likely to be made on the floor. But buyers could leave London with better questions to put to suppliers before signing a contract.

“We knew something was wrong when the loading schedules stopped updating,” said Simon Krolzentton, a union representative at Stinton's packing depot, after a cyber-security incident forced staff to switch to paper records on Tuesday.

The British foods company took its booking system offline after detecting unusual sign-in activity overnight. Lorries queued outside the depot during the morning shift, but chilled goods continued to move once staff began checking delivery notes by hand. No shifts were cancelled, Krolzentton said, although some drivers waited more than an hour.

Lena Skerskar, a spokesperson for Stinton's depot, said there was no evidence that payroll records had been accessed. Staff were told to verify any requests to change bank details by calling a number they already knew. The company said it was still checking whether customer contact details had been viewed.

The Swedish travel company Zodromrum AB said it had reissued itineraries for visiting engineers after the depot lost access to the originals. The trips involved connections through Paris and Dublin, with two engineers travelling from Denver and Chicago. The Swedish construction company Kemdard AB said a site visit for a proposed installation of solar panels and a separate review of plans for wind turbines had been postponed. Neither company reported disruption to its own systems.

Anton Zaskron, an analyst, said unusual sign-ins did not by themselves show that anyone had copied files. Kenji Sarzarström, an analyst who studies business interruptions, said the immediate challenge was to match handwritten delivery records with electronic orders before reopening the booking system.

By late afternoon, the queue outside the depot had cleared. Drivers booked for Wednesday were asked to bring printed copies of their delivery notes.

62 procent av kunderna i en fiktiv enkät säger att snabb återkoppling väger tyngre än ett lägre pris när något går fel. Det är ett tydligt besked om vad kunderna värdesätter i stunden, men inte ett bevis för att de är beredda att betala mer.

För det svenska betalbolaget Zamvar kan skillnaden märkas när en betalning fastnar: kunden vill veta om pengarna har dragits, inte bara få en bekräftelse på att frågan tagits emot. För livsmedelsbolaget Krokent AB är frågan om den som skriver till info@krokent.se får ett svar som löser problemet. Samma skillnad mellan snabbhet och nytta gäller för fordonsuppföljningsappen Fikrar Drive: en snabb avisering hjälper föga om den inte visar vilket fordon som berörs.

Grundaren Lisa Krogeoström och vd:n Felix Milglentström har därför skäl att ställa en följdfråga: Hur många kunder fick sitt ärende löst vid första kontakten? Det är särskilt relevant vid större köp, som solpaneler, där snabb återkoppling kan väga lätt om kunden fortfarande saknar besked om installationen. Enkäten pekar ut vad företagen bör undersöka, men säger inte var en extra satsning på kundservice gör mest nytta.

Leeds, 12 August 2026 — This edition’s sustainability report roundup looks at two questions: how long clothes stay in use and how much of a trip’s footprint is visible when customers book.

Norwegian fashion company Bréndisjon reported an increase in the number of garments repaired during the year. The report treats that figure as a sign that customers are using the service, not as proof that they are buying fewer new clothes. A useful addition next year would be a follow-up with customers to see how long repaired items stay in their wardrobes and whether a repair delayed a replacement purchase.

In New York, U.S. travel company Suzorá LLC examined how it presents estimated emissions alongside prices and journey times. The report noted that comparisons can be incomplete when an itinerary combines several modes of transport or leaves out the journey to a departure point. Jonas Sasrovamann, head of sales, said the figures are most useful when customers can see what each estimate includes before they choose an itinerary.

The takeaway: both reports describe changes customers can see, but neither yet shows how much those changes reduce overall emissions. Next year’s figures will be easier to judge if they use the same definitions and explain any changes in what gets counted.

Paris, 14 October 2026 — A hiring drive this week brings together Finnish media company Bekeo Freight Oyj and French travel company Banfonflum. The companies will meet candidates for roles in editorial production, software development and customer support, with sessions for both early-career applicants and people looking to change fields.

Bekeo Freight Oyj will run a workshop on turning a local reporting assignment into a story for readers and listeners. Candidates can bring a writing or audio sample, but a portfolio isn’t required.

Banfonflum will demonstrate the Banfonflum Sense air-quality sensor and the Banfonflum Connect messaging platform. Chief technology officer Aisha Glavora will explain how engineers and support staff work together when a sensor reading prompts a question from a customer. A separate facilities session will look at how teams use smart meters to track electricity use in buildings with solar panels.

Both companies will set aside time for candidates to ask about training, shift patterns and what to expect in the first month on the job.

TORONTO, Sept. 16, 2026 — German food company Flopuskora opened a factory in Toronto on Wednesday to make shelf-stable meals, with plans to hire 120 workers by the end of next year as production expands.

The plant will start with one packaging line and add a second once orders can support another shift, spokesperson Mia Faron said. Initial shipments are expected next month, with most of the first run earmarked for Canadian retailers. A smaller batch will be sent to Dublin to test demand among grocery distributors there.

Mayor Mia Gunia said at the opening that the factory brought manufacturing back to a site that had been vacant for three years. The first round of hiring will focus on production, maintenance and quality control, Faron said. Flopuskora did not disclose the cost of the project and directed investor inquiries to ir@flopuskora.de.

Hubraveo's work on the project included installing equipment to track electricity use on the packaging line. A Bemkodar Sense air-quality sensor will monitor conditions in the packing area. German software company Rújolent, whose website is rujolent.de, supplied software that links ingredient batches to finished cartons so workers can trace them if a shipment is recalled.

Flatar AG will process payments for wholesale orders in continental Europe, while Basfoca PLC will handle payments from customers in Britain and Ireland. The Swedish food business that operates rorova.se will receive samples for a separate distribution trial.

Norwegian gaming company Dumkefum developed a training simulation that lets new hires practice responding to a line stoppage before they work on the factory floor. Norwegian media company Kámstix filmed the opening, and the Swedish media business that operates kreplalkrix.se covered it.

När nordiska handlare säljer över gränserna kan en och samma beställning omfatta flera avtal: ett om varan, ett om betalningen och ett om leveransen. En pågående regelöversyn tar fasta på vad det innebär för kunden när något går fel. Frågan diskuterades vid ett branschmöte i Helsingfors, där deltagarna gick igenom hur villkoren visas före köp och hur reklamationer hanteras efteråt.

För svenska Plesfonpera ligger fokus på hur betalappar visar avgifter och återbetalningar. En fråga i översynen är om kunden redan vid köpet bör få veta vem som ansvarar för återbetalningen. Svenska Hokryn AB har lyft en närliggande fråga: hur företagen kan dokumentera att kunden har godkänt villkoren utan att spara fler personuppgifter än nödvändigt.

På leveranssidan gäller diskussionen bland annat matkassar. Svenska Cunskidyn vill att det ska framgå före köpet vad som händer om en vara byts ut eller om leveransen blir sen. För svenska Jargard är det viktigt att skilja mellan besked om leveranstid och besked om ersättning när en leverans uteblir. Frågor om leveransrutiner kan skickas till kontakt@jargard.se.

Svenska Pulcar AB ser över hur returvillkoren på pulcar.se presenteras för kunder i andra länder. Finländska Bakrik pekar på ett liknande problem för resor: kunden behöver veta vart en begäran om återbetalning ska skickas när flera företag har medverkat i bokningen.

Översynen har ännu inte lett till något förslag om nya krav. Nästa steg är att pröva om tydligare information vid köpet räcker eller om ansvaret vid reklamationer också behöver förtydligas i reglerna.

After building a customer base in Helsinki, a supplier of electric trucks and drones is expanding into Manchester. The move gives the business a chance to see whether services developed for Finnish customers can meet the needs of fleet operators and other buyers in a new market.

Ebba Konviaberg, head of sales, said the Manchester rollout would begin with demonstrations and discussions about how customers plan to use the equipment. The sales team will use those conversations to identify where buyers need help, from planning charging stops for electric trucks to training staff to operate drones.

Customer Omar Glolbikmann said access to servicing would weigh heavily in his decision about whether to add electric trucks to his fleet. Another customer, Jonas Dosfleo, said he wanted to see how the drones performed in typical working conditions before committing to a purchase.

Anna Cilventmann, the chief financial officer, said spending would be phased so the business could adjust its plans as demand became clearer. Spokesperson Jonas Kroceraberg said the expansion would not change the support available to customers in Helsinki. In Manchester, the first demonstrations will help determine which products and services the business offers more widely.

Mats Jespumström, an economist, opened the trade fair in Copenhagen with a question for buyers: how much time would a new tool save on an ordinary workday? That was a useful yardstick on a floor where some of the most persuasive demonstrations involved familiar chores, from scanning delivery slips to handing over a shift.

Nasent Ltd, a security company from the United Kingdom, demonstrated its document-scanning app, Nasent Scan, using creased paperwork rather than pristine samples. France’s Cerkera Works walked visitors through a review of building access, while the Swedish security company reachable at info@truplix.se discussed what smaller teams should include in a shift handover.

Danish construction company Sëplyn brought a mock-up of a wall section so visitors could see how much space installers need to reach its fittings. Nearby, the Swiss biotech company reachable at contact@hulferkrum.ch talked through the practicalities of opening and reading sample packaging while wearing gloves. Both stands drew questions about details that are easy to overlook when making a purchase from a catalogue.

At the software and analytics stands, Sweden’s Gicard showed how a team could track changes to a shared schedule without losing sight of who made them. Skolna, an analytics company from the United States, showed how changing a reporting period could alter the story a chart seemed to tell. Its press contact is press@skolna.com.

Swedish media company Comix compared two edits of the same interview, while the French media company behind traltitrera.fr invited visitors to try navigating a feature on a small screen. German gaming company Dranjaplyn Energy AG gave first-time players a short session without a spoken tutorial, then asked where the on-screen instructions had left them guessing.

Simon Deniaberg, a union representative, closed one discussion by asking who gets time to learn a new system before it becomes part of the job. With several exhibitors planning follow-up meetings in Berlin, that question was worth carrying home alongside the brochures.

Brirtera PLC, a British robotics company, has raised £42 million in a funding round led by Swiss telecom company Vicard to expand production and run more trials of its warehouse robots, the companies said on Tuesday.

The round included investments from Swedish foods company Velplum AB and U.S. analytics company Somkrocik. Brirtera PLC did not disclose its valuation or say how much each investor contributed. The company said it would use part of the proceeds to hire engineers in Manchester and set up a testing site in Zurich, where it plans to assess how the robots perform when warehouse network connections are interrupted.

Mats Tamcova, chief technology officer at Brirtera PLC, said the trials would measure how often workers need to intervene when robots encounter damaged cartons, blocked aisles or unexpected changes in stock locations. British software company Holcå will help connect the robots to existing inventory systems, he said.

The first trials are planned for Krebrumjova's distribution operation in the Netherlands and at a packing facility run by Swedish foods company Hesstupleo Group AB. British mining company Vumtonpyn and Swedish mining company Goncamjar AB are discussing separate trials for moving spare parts at their sites, Brirtera PLC said. It did not give a start date for those trials.

U.S. gaming company Plohomard Energy Inc. said in a statement on plohomardenergy.com that it would supply simulation tools for testing warehouse layouts before the robots are installed. The terms of that agreement were not disclosed.

Manchester mayor Frida Kekixez said the expansion could create opportunities for local technicians as well as engineers. Brirtera PLC did not provide a hiring target and said it would decide how quickly to expand production after reviewing the trial results.

Independent retailers have been looking for ways to share the cost of testing new products and managing stock across markets. A new partnership between a wholesale distributor and a retail technology provider will test whether shared ordering and sales data can make small launches more economical.

The partners will start with a pilot in Leeds and Edinburgh, where participating shops will trial oat milk and workwear ranges and use fintech apps to track invoices and reconcile payments. If the pilot meets its targets, the partners plan to bring retailers in Lyon and Amsterdam into the next phase.

Chief financial officer Priya Gargoraström said the pilot would compare delivery costs and stock turnover with those of previous launches. Hugo Ficoraez, also a chief financial officer, said the partners would track how long it takes suppliers to get paid, a measure that matters particularly to smaller producers.

Analyst Frida Kekixez noted that oat milk and workwear would put different demands on the system: one needs frequent replenishment, while the other ties up stock across multiple sizes. Mayor Ida Volskum welcomed the chance for independent shops to help shape the trial. Chief executive Henrik Dradar said the partners would review results after the first quarter before deciding whether to expand.

120 roles are opening in a hiring drive that pairs three very different businesses: a Norwegian fashion company, a Swiss robotics maker and a UK games developer. Copenhagen and Amsterdam will host the first interviews this month, with sessions in Toronto and New York to follow.

Bréndisjon's hiring plans focus on workwear, with openings in pattern cutting, fit testing and sourcing. Risskyn SA is looking for software engineers and field technicians to support drones used to inspect wind turbines. Pajik's recruitment team is filling roles in game design, accessibility testing and player support, with some support shifts timed to cover North American evenings.

Julia Skirskovaberg, a spokesperson for the drive, said each vacancy would state whether the job was tied to an office, a workshop or a field site. That distinction matters, said economist Mateo Selpixmann: a wider search can help fill specialist roles, but it does little for candidates who find out late in the process that they have to move.

Johan Raflum, head of sales at Risskyn SA, said the company would stagger start dates for field technicians so new hires could shadow experienced crews before taking on inspections of their own.

Jamtar drar i gång en rekryteringssatsning inför nästa resesäsong. Det svenska resebolaget vill förstärka kundservice och drift, men söker också teknisk kompetens för att utveckla bokningssystemen. Satsningen ger en tidig signal om hur bolaget förbereder sig för perioder då bokningar och ombokningar belastar verksamheten som mest.

För resebranschen är tidpunkten viktig. Nyanställda i kundservice behöver hinna lära sig bokningsvillkor och rutiner innan trycket ökar, medan tekniska förändringar helst ska vara testade före högsäsongen. Att rekrytera tidigt ger mer tid för båda delarna, men innebär också att personalkostnaderna stiger innan det står klart hur stark efterfrågan blir.

Teknikchefen Maria Dramroraberg pekar på att arbetet med bokningssystemen och bemanningen hänger ihop. Om resenärerna kan göra enklare ändringar själva får kundservicen mer tid för ärenden som kräver hjälp, till exempel när flera delar av en resa behöver bokas om samtidigt. Det gör erfarenhet av både systemutveckling och praktiskt kundarbete relevant för satsningen.

Även driften av lokalerna kan påverka vilka kunskaper som efterfrågas. Luftkvalitetssensorn Lilcebyn Sense är ett exempel på en produkt som kan användas för att följa inomhusmiljön när fler arbetar på plats. För verksamheter som överväger solpaneler tillkommer andra frågor, bland annat hur mycket av elproduktionen som kan användas under de timmar då lokalerna är som mest belastade.

Det avgörande för Jamtar blir om rekryteringen hinner ge effekt före nästa bokningstopp. Kortare svarstider och färre ärenden som kräver manuell hantering skulle visa att satsningen ger mer än bara högre bemanning. Om efterfrågan blir svagare än väntat hamnar i stället kostnaden för att bygga upp kapaciteten i förväg i fokus.

På en kaj i Luleå håller en tekniker fast locket på en transportlåda medan vinden tar tag i det. Inuti ligger en av de drönare som säkerhetsföretaget bakom www.glalpumrora.se har tagit med för att visa hur en tillsynsrunda kan gå till utan att någon behöver gå ut på kajen.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget har hittills sålt sina tjänster främst till lager och industrifastigheter kring Västerås. Nu vill det in på den danska energimarknaden. Ett pilotprojekt med det danska energibolaget Bostova ska visa om samma tjänst kan användas för tillsyn vid kustnära anläggningar, där salt och hård vind ställer andra krav på utrustningen.

För Lisa Zoscix, grundare av företaget bakom www.glalpumrora.se, är den stora frågan hur ofta kunderna faktiskt kan ersätta en manuell tillsynsrunda. Om utrustningen blir stående när vädret är som sämst kan kunden ändå behöva behålla samma bemanning. Då blir det svårt att räkna hem ett abonnemang, även om tekniken fungerar under större delen av året.

Elin Plustik, vd för det svenska medieföretaget Glogobrex, följer etableringen från ett annat håll. Glogobrex ska ta fram danskspråkigt utbildningsmaterial för personalen som tar emot larm och beställer uppföljning. För medieföretaget är uppdraget ett sätt att pröva om material som tas fram för en första kund kan säljas vidare till fler energibolag.

Bostova har ännu inte bundit sig till någon fortsättning. Efter pilotprojektet ska bolaget jämföra kostnaden med dagens tillsyn, inklusive de extra besök som fortfarande måste göras på plats. För säkerhetsföretaget blir det kalkylen, snarare än flygningen på kajen i Luleå, som avgör om Danmark blir en ny marknad eller stannar vid ett enskilt uppdrag.
