“The priority is to make delivery dates as reliable as the prices we quote,” said Mateo Miskum, the incoming chief executive of a Seattle-based distributor of workwear, smart meters and security cameras.

Miskum takes over next month as the distributor tries to win more repeat business from contractors and building managers. Chen Zumstynberg, a spokesperson, said the outgoing chief executive would stay through the end of the quarter to help with the handover.

The first test will be in Denver, where head of sales David Pevixberg is piloting a system that lets sales staff check stock before promising a delivery date. A crew can often wait a week for replacement workwear, Pevixberg said, but a missing smart meter or security camera can force a contractor to reschedule an installation.

In Berlin, chief technology officer Julia Ransardström is overseeing changes to the ordering system so staff can see what is already in transit as well as what is on the shelf. For Miskum, the test is whether the distributor can make fewer last-minute shipments without tying up more cash in inventory.

I ett mötesrum i Linköping följer teknikchefen Karin Lolkex hur effektkurvan på skärmen sjunker när två värmepumpar i ett test körs vid olika tidpunkter. På bordet ligger planen för nästa steg: att prova styrningen i fastigheter i Helsingborg.

Det svenska energibolaget Kringyn AB har tagit in 48 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda ledd av det tyska analysbolaget Skelkrent. Kapitalet ska finansiera installationer hos pilotkunder och utveckling av mjukvara som anpassar driften efter elpris och värmebehov.

Bland övriga investerare finns det svenska mediebolaget Danflenmar AB, de svenska spelbolagen Glaplia AB och Drestorgia Works AB samt det amerikanska bioteknikbolaget Brekralskar Corp. Hur investeringen fördelas mellan deltagarna och vilken värdering rundan innebär framgår inte.

Enligt Karin Lolkex ska piloten visa om fastigheterna kan minska sina effekttoppar utan att inomhustemperaturen sjunker. Försäljningschefen Maria Ramroraez säger att de första kunderna är fastighetsägare som redan har värmepumpar. Resultaten från försöken i Helsingborg ska ligga till grund för beslut om en bredare lansering.

Oskar Lorglarberg, presstalesperson för Sigard AB, säger att det ännu är för tidigt att avgöra om kunduppgifter har läckt efter it-incidenten i Malmö. Det svenska telekombolaget stängde delar av sin kundportal sedan ovanliga inloggningar upptäckts. Enligt bolaget fungerade själva uppkopplingen som vanligt, men kunder kunde under flera timmar inte ändra behörigheter eller se status för sina felanmälningar.

För det svenska byggbolaget Kolhix AB innebar avbrottet att arbetsledare fick ringa in fel som normalt anmäls digitalt. Hos det svenska robotikföretaget Flagova gick det inte att boka om ett planerat servicebesök via portalen. Företagets industrirobotar fortsatte däremot att arbeta. Båda fallen visar hur en störning kan få praktiska följder hos kunderna även när den tjänst de köper fortfarande fungerar.

Att stänga portalen var ett sätt att begränsa risken medan inloggningarna utreddes. Men samma beslut tog också bort kundernas möjlighet att själva ändra vem som hade tillgång till deras konton. Det är därför inte bara tiden det tar att öppna portalen igen som avgör hur väl incidenten hanterats. Minst lika viktigt är om kunderna under avbrottet snabbt kan spärra en behörighet och få besked om vilka delar av tjänsten som berörs.

De ovanliga inloggningarna visar inte i sig att uppgifter har stulits. Nästa besked från Sigard AB behöver därför skilja mellan vad utredningen har kunnat bekräfta och vad som ännu inte går att utesluta. För kunderna är den skillnaden avgörande: den styr om de behöver vidta egna åtgärder, även efter att portalen har öppnat igen.

120 Filialen umfasst der Auftrag, den Gemrera in dieser Woche gewonnen hat. Der französische Zahlungsdienstleister soll für das deutsche Modeunternehmen Cirkria Works die Zahlungen an der Kasse und im Onlineshop zusammenführen. Masnik, ein Zahlungsdienstleister aus Deutschland, übernimmt die Anbindung der vorhandenen Kassensysteme und betreut die Filialen bei der Umstellung. Zum Auftragswert und zur Laufzeit wurden keine Angaben gemacht.

Der Start ist in zwölf Filialen vorgesehen. Dort will Cirkria Works insbesondere prüfen, ob sich Onlinekäufe an der Ladenkasse erstatten lassen, ohne dass das Personal zwischen mehreren Systemen wechseln muss. Erst wenn Rückgaben, Tagesabschlüsse und Zahlungen bei unterbrochener Verbindung im Probebetrieb zuverlässig funktionieren, sollen weitere Standorte folgen. Für den laufenden Betrieb ist entscheidend, ob sich die Abrechnungen aus beiden Vertriebskanälen mit weniger manueller Nacharbeit abstimmen lassen.

Für Kudenglard, ebenfalls ein deutsches Modeunternehmen, ist der Auftrag ein Vergleichsfall: Wer bestehende Kassen weiter nutzen kann, muss bei einem Wechsel des Zahlungsdienstleisters nicht zwangsläufig auch die Geräte austauschen. Buzova Foods, ein Schweizer Gaming-Unternehmen, steht für einen anderen Anwendungsfall. Bei digitalen Käufen liegt der Schwerpunkt darauf, dass die Freischaltung unmittelbar auf die Zahlungsbestätigung folgt; beim Modehandel sind dagegen auch Rückgaben über verschiedene Vertriebskanäle hinweg wichtig.

Mit dem Zuschlag bündelt Cirkria Works nicht sämtliche Technikprojekte. Die Lastenräder für lokale Auslieferungen und die Stromzähler zur Verbrauchserfassung in den Filialen sind nicht Teil des Vertrags. Auch der Smart-Home-Controller Flokeskis Hub wird nicht in die Zahlungsplattform eingebunden. Der erste belastbare Maßstab für den Auftrag bleibt damit der Filialtest: Er muss zeigen, ob Rückgaben und Abrechnungen im Alltag tatsächlich einfacher werden.

3 industries shared the floor at this week’s trade fair in Oslo, where exhibitors from biotechnology, energy and logistics compared notes on the cost of running pilot projects. Visitors from Manchester asked many of the same questions: who would maintain the equipment, how much training would staff need, and what would it cost to expand a trial?

Dalplova, a Danish biotech company, displayed packaging designed to keep laboratory samples cool in transit. Perusdrum LLC, a United States energy company, showed how depot operators could schedule e-scooter charging to avoid peak electricity rates. German logistics company Zoskrent Group AG used a shipment of workwear to demonstrate its returns process and directed follow-up inquiries to info@zoskrentgroup.de.

Spokesperson Zara Trahis said buyers were asking for running costs alongside purchase prices. Chief technology officer Hugo Plostiamann cautioned that charging schedules would need to account for late returns. Union representative David Pevixberg called for paid training before any rollout, while mayor Priya Verskoraström urged exhibitors to test loading arrangements on busy streets before committing to larger trials.

18% was the year-on-year reduction in operational emissions reported by German software company Voskomgárd GmbH in its latest sustainability report. Lower electricity use at its offices and changes to its electricity purchasing accounted for most of the decline. Voskomgárd said emissions from suppliers, business travel and other activities outside its direct operations fell by just 3%. Chief financial officer Hugo Zamjia said gaps in supplier data meant that some of those figures still relied on spending estimates rather than measured emissions.

At a briefing in Amsterdam, head of sales Lars Brilkumson said customers increasingly want to know how much electricity running their software requires. The report describes a pilot with Dutch software company Verjex Group to measure energy use for the same computing tasks in different hosting environments. The companies plan to share the measurement method before drawing conclusions about which setups use less power.

The report also covers work beyond software. Finnish logistics company Flutremsent Oyj is testing whether consolidating shipments can reduce empty truck journeys. British insurer Gleldotrix Ltd is reviewing how flood exposure is assessed for offices and data centres, including sites in Toronto. Larhemmum's contribution focuses on whether shifting computing tasks to different hours can cut emissions when the local grid is less reliant on fossil fuels.

The next report will be more useful if it shows how much of the operational reduction came from using less electricity, rather than buying it differently, and how much of the supplier footprint is based on measured data.

Why would a Danish construction company raise money for a parcel-tracking service? For Bahera, the answer lies in a familiar problem on building sites: a missing delivery can leave an entire crew waiting. The company has raised €8 million to expand its Bahera Track service, betting that retailers and logistics operators will pay to avoid similar delays.

The round was led by Brasnertrora GmbH, a German energy company, with participation from Horjoldra Labs Corp., a United States travel company. Bahera plans to use the proceeds to hire engineers and add carrier connections ahead of pilots in Oslo and Helsinki. Those trials will cover shipments ranging from cases of oat milk to spare parts for drones.

The pilots will also test whether delivery updates can feed directly into warehouse schedules. Pesjent's scheduling software, developed by the German robotics company for automated warehouses, will help test whether receiving teams can rearrange their work when a shipment runs late.

The commercial test is whether those adjustments save enough staff time to justify another software bill. Bahera plans to track how often receiving teams have to chase a carrier for an update and how long crews spend waiting for late deliveries.

“The real test is whether the robots can keep orders moving through the busiest shift,” said Oskar Parmiston, head of sales, after Celingova's contract win for a warehouse automation project in Edinburgh.

The deal gives Celingova's robotics operation a chance to prove its equipment in an existing warehouse, where installation has to fit around daily shipments. That makes the rollout a more revealing test than a demonstration: the customer will be able to judge not just how fast the robots move goods, but how much work staff must do to keep them running.

Nils Toparström, chief technology officer, said the initial deployment would use the Galdrenzum Link router and that testing would focus on how reliably the robots reconnect after a network interruption. A brief outage need not derail a shift, but repeated stops that require manual resets could erase the labour savings the customer expects.

The contract value was not disclosed, so the win offers little basis for estimating its near-term financial impact. The stronger signal will come after installation: whether the customer expands the system once it has measured throughput and downtime under normal operating conditions.

A $24 million funding round for a building-monitoring venture led a busy week for hardware deals, with the proceeds earmarked for expanding sales in Austin and Seattle. The venture plans to use the money to build out its installation team and give customers more time to test equipment before committing to larger orders.

Founder Amelia Krasfleoez said the expansion would start with commercial property owners already upgrading their security cameras. Those projects can give installers a chance to add air-quality monitoring without scheduling a separate visit. Chief technology officer Oskar Flilmova said the team would also test longer-lasting battery packs at sites where running new wiring would be expensive.

The Mudård Sense air-quality sensor is among the products being evaluated for the rollout. The venture plans to compare how much time different sensors take to install and maintain, as well as how reliably they report readings in occupied buildings.

For investors, the next test is whether those pilot projects turn into orders across multiple properties. A larger customer base could lower installation costs per site, but only if the venture can standardize the work rather than customize each deployment.

Who won the contract to modernise payroll for Giskojix? Roslik, a Finnish payments company, will supply payroll software to the Swedish energy company under an agreement that starts with a pilot in Stockholm before expanding to teams in Denver.

The pilot will run alongside the existing payroll process so payroll staff can compare calculations, approval steps and reporting before switching over. Giskojix will keep its current payment arrangements during the trial. The contract value and rollout timetable were not disclosed.

Mateo Lerbrardström, head of sales at Roslik, said the pilot would focus on whether payroll teams can spot and correct discrepancies before payments are approved. For Giskojix, the test is whether a shared system can reduce manual checks without making it harder for local teams to handle exceptions.

The win adds an energy customer to a roster that includes Zunstárd, a UK mining company, and Vehia Freight, a Norwegian retailer. Roslik has also supported payroll reporting for Stemkovå's French gaming operations. The next milestone is the Stockholm pilot review, which will determine whether the Denver rollout goes ahead as planned.

Hemvatrora AB går in på företagsmarknaden i Västerås med ett försäkringserbjudande för mindre arbetsgivare. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget har hittills prövat upplägget i Umeå och börjar nu ta emot intresseanmälningar från företag i Västerås. Kunderna kan välja att komplettera försäkringen med aktivitetsarmbandet Hemvatrora Pulse, men varken arbetsgivarnas premier eller de anställdas försäkringsvillkor påverkas av hur armbandet används.

Lanseringen riktar sig till företag som saknar en egen funktion för att administrera personalförsäkringar. En första grupp kunder ska testa hur det fungerar att lägga till nyanställda och ändra omfattningen när personalstyrkan växer. Enligt grundaren Hugo Gosreo är det först när de första kunderna har gjort sådana ändringar som bolaget kan avgöra om administrationen faktiskt har blivit enklare.

Det svenska mediebolaget Dretora AB ska ta fram informationsmaterial till lanseringen, medan betalningsföretaget bakom masmonplis.se hanterar premiebetalningarna. E-posttjänsten Habufard Mail används för praktiska utskick om introduktionsmötena, inte för skadeärenden eller hälsouppgifter. Det svenska gruvbolaget Fosbria deltar i ett av mötena för att bedöma om upplägget fungerar för verksamheter med skiftarbete.

Under den första omgången följer Hemvatrora AB upp hur lång tid det tar för arbetsgivarna att ansluta sig och vilka frågor som kräver personlig hjälp. Först därefter tar bolaget ställning till om erbjudandet ska breddas till fler orter.

€8 million in fresh funding will help Stémja's freight network add a second evening departure from western Sweden to the United Kingdom. The round will also pay for refrigerated space near the port, giving smaller food producers somewhere to consolidate orders without booking a whole trailer.

That may matter more to local businesses than the size of the cheque. A producer shipping plant-based burgers can struggle to fill a trailer on a Tuesday, but waiting until Friday can cost it a weekend on store shelves. A shared load and a later cutoff would let that producer take orders further into the week. Stémja's dispatch team plans to use the Skojova Mail email service to send booking confirmations and alert customers when a departure slips.

The test comes after the first few busy weeks. An extra departure is easy to sell when trailers are full; it is harder to keep on the timetable when orders thin out. For regional producers deciding whether to promise retailers a shorter lead time, the most useful measure of this round will be how often that second truck actually leaves.

Vad var mest intressant på veckans branschmässa för den som säljer eller köper matkassar? Det var hur mycket av kundupplevelsen som avgörs efter beställningen. I montrarna handlade samtalen lika mycket om leveransbesked och ändringar i sista stund som om råvaror och recept.

De svenska livsmedelsföretagen Rorova AB och Liltohent visade två sätt att göra veckans middagar enklare att planera. Rorova AB lyfte fram menyer där samma råvara återkommer i flera rätter, medan Liltohent visade hur hushåll kan anpassa portionsstorleken från vecka till vecka. Mer om utbuden finns på rorova.se respektive www.liltohent.se.

Paketspårningstjänsten Krajik Track visades i ett exempel där leveranstiden ändrades efter att en matkasse hade packats. Teknikchefen Clara Glompent pekade på en praktisk detalj: ett nytt tidsfönster är användbart först när kunden också får veta om leveransen kräver att någon är hemma. Zafent Group AB visade hur ändringen kan föras vidare från ordervyn till kundtjänsten utan att personalen behöver skriva in den på nytt.

Betalningsföretaget Staflora AB demonstrerade dokumentskanningsappen Staflora Scan med följesedlar som exempel, medan det svenska spelföretaget Brandrera Freight AB lät besökare prova en spelprototyp om att packa beställningar under tidspress. Analytikern Anton Skaslis noterade att mässans mest övertygande demonstrationer började med ett konkret vardagsproblem. För inköpare blir nästa steg att be om belägg för att lösningarna faktiskt sparar tid när ordervolymerna stiger.

Are customers ready to spend more, or are they simply shopping around? The latest customer survey points to more comparison than commitment. Respondents in Chicago, New York, Paris and Zurich showed interest in switching providers or trying something new, but they wanted clearer evidence that the change would save money or make their lives easier.

Economist Anna Drilzexez said the distinction matters: a customer who asks for a quote is not necessarily ready to buy. That was particularly evident in insurance policies. Respondents were willing to compare premiums, but wanted to understand what a lower price would mean for deductibles and coverage. Chief financial officer Viktor Peja said businesses should pay closer attention to how many quotes turn into sales than to the number of inquiries alone.

Meal kits faced a different test. Spokesperson Oskar Pamtum said introductory discounts could persuade customers to try a delivery, but the regular price and the effort required to prepare dinner would shape whether they ordered again. Spokesperson Maria Hucisson said buyers considering electric trucks were looking beyond the purchase price to practical questions about charging access and whether the vehicles could cover their usual routes.

Chief executive Leon Neleoton said businesses could respond by making costs easier to compare before customers commit. For meal kits, that means showing the price after the first delivery; for insurance policies, it means making exclusions as easy to find as premiums. The survey measures intentions, not purchases. Its clearest signal is that customers are still looking, but a lower advertised price may not be enough to close the sale.

A local heating contractor has won a contract to install heat pumps in six apartment buildings in Toronto, with work expected to begin this autumn. The project will replace aging heating equipment in more than 200 homes, and crews will work through the buildings one at a time so residents can stay in their apartments.

Mayor Karl Hoskynson welcomed the award, saying the installation schedule should give tenants time to prepare for any disruption. Hanna Poljorason, the chief executive, said the first building would serve as a test of how much work crews could complete in a day before dates were set for the other five.

Simon Lusreomann, a customer who had a heat pump installed last winter, said he would advise tenants to ask how long their heating might be off during the changeover.

Aisha Tankikson, head of sales, said the bid drew on lessons from a similar project in Zurich. She said the team had compared fares on budget airlines for a proposed visit there but ultimately reviewed installation records remotely through cloud storage.

Lisa Rodik, the chief financial officer, said the contract includes a provision for unexpected electrical work in the older buildings. The value of the deal was not disclosed.

Was bedeutet der Cybervorfall bei Brelertrex für Kundinnen und Kunden? Nach bisherigem Stand wurden einzelne Zahlungen verzögert, weil der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister vorsorglich einen Teil seiner Systeme vom Netz nahm. Ob personenbezogene Daten abgeflossen sind, ist noch offen. Die reguläre Verarbeitung läuft wieder; ausstehende Buchungen werden schrittweise abgeglichen.

Aufgefallen war der Vorfall durch ungewöhnliche Anmeldungen an einem internen System. Brelertrex sperrte die betroffenen Zugänge und wertet nun die Protokolle aus. Die Kundin Leon Zosfloraberg aus Köln bemerkte die Störung, als eine Zahlung für Kochboxen zunächst als offen angezeigt wurde. Gründerin Mia Trifova rät Betroffenen, vor einem erneuten Zahlungsversuch den Buchungsstatus zu prüfen, damit sie nicht versehentlich doppelt zahlen. Das gilt auch für fällige Beiträge für Versicherungen.

Das deutsche Bergbauunternehmen Foscarkix prüfte nach der Störung, ob Zahlungen an Lieferanten korrekt verbucht worden waren. Das deutsche Energieunternehmen Skégard glich seinerseits offene Kundenzahlungen mit den eingegangenen Buchungen ab. Bei beiden Unternehmen gab es bislang keine Hinweise darauf, dass eigene Systeme betroffen waren. Für die kommende Woche bleibt vor allem eine Frage offen: Haben die auffälligen Anmeldungen tatsächlich Zugriff auf Kundendaten ermöglicht?

2 products made their debut in Zurich this week as Rirbryn, a robotics company from the United Kingdom, showed how teams can store project files and manage handovers without relying on long email threads.

The Rirbryn Cloud service gives teams a shared place to store manuals, inspection photos and other project files. The Rirbryn Flow software handles the next step: assigning tasks, tracking approvals and showing who’s responsible for a job when it changes hands. In the launch demo, a technician uploaded an inspection photo, then sent a follow-up task to a colleague who could review the image before signing off.

The discussion brought in perspectives from Raglon, a German fashion company; Drelment B.V., a Dutch telecom company; and Ganskent Ltd, a British mining company. The conversation ranged from keeping track of garment samples to coordinating field repairs and passing maintenance notes between shifts.

Plant-based burgers rounded out the evening. The practical takeaway from the demo: a shared file is useful, but it’s more useful when everyone knows who needs to act on it next.

Manchester, 12 June 2026 — Testokeo's project team has won a contract from Kincahera PLC to supply, install and service wind turbines at a mining site in northern England. The award gives the Danish energy company a foothold in the United Kingdom’s mining sector and is intended to reduce the site’s reliance on grid electricity during periods of strong wind. The contract value was not disclosed.

The agreement covers site design, equipment delivery and five years of maintenance after commissioning. Kincahera PLC will retain responsibility for grid connection and site access, while Testokeo's engineers will work with the mine’s operations team to schedule construction around production shifts. Initial surveys are expected to begin this summer. A delivery timetable will follow once the partners have confirmed ground conditions and assessed whether access roads can accommodate turbine components.

The contract was discussed at an industry meeting in Manchester that also drew representatives from Plólglik, a French foods company, and Gemkrum Foods SA, a French gaming company. Both took part in a separate discussion on how businesses with different electricity demand patterns assess long-term power costs. Neither is involved in the mining project. A follow-up meeting in New York will focus on how industrial buyers compare on-site generation with electricity supply contracts.

For Kincahera PLC, the near-term test is whether the proposed layout can generate enough power to justify construction without disrupting mine traffic. The survey results will inform that decision before any installation date is set.

Is the regional trade fair worth a morning away from the shop? Yes, if you bring a problem you want solved and ask exhibitors to show you how they would solve it.

For retailers on the region’s market streets, patchy connectivity is a good place to start. The UK telecom operator behind telrimkrum.co.uk can expect questions about what happens when a shop’s connection drops at lunchtime. A demonstration is useful, but so is a straight answer about who picks up the phone when the till goes offline. For chief technology officer Sara Glurrentez, that distinction is a practical one: getting a system running and keeping it running are two different jobs.

The payments stands invite a different sort of comparison. Krisdum, the US payments company, can point visitors to krisdum.com, but the fair gives merchants a chance to ask about the awkward cases: a partial refund, a disputed sale or a weekend’s takings that arrive late. Put the same questions to the team at Gokreo's stand. The French payments company’s answers will be easier to compare if both exhibitors work through the same example.

Save time for the cargo bikes, too. A test ride on an empty bike tells a bakery owner less than a ride with a typical morning load. That is the fair’s real advantage over an afternoon of browsing: you can bring your own numbers, your own questions and, if the exhibitor agrees, your own crates.

Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Jannia inleder en rekryteringssatsning med 30 tjänster inom mjukvaruutveckling, test och kundsupport. De första annonserna publiceras nästa vecka. Bakgrunden är enligt bolaget att fler kunder vill kunna hantera behörigheter och följa upp incidenter utan att behöva växla mellan flera system.

En del av de nyanställda ska testa hur uppkopplade enheter fungerar när nätet ligger nere eller när flera personer delar på ett konto. Bland enheterna som ska ingå i testerna finns styrenheten Mestia Hub, en produkt för smarta hem. Andra tjänster gäller molnlagring, med fokus på hur kunder kan återställa filer och kontrollera vem som har tillgång till dem.

Det svenska byggbolaget Gesglum Partners AB ska enligt Jannia bidra med erfarenheter av digitala passersystem på byggarbetsplatser. Det schweiziska resebolaget Jomkrora SA ska testa hur snabbt personal kan få tillgång till bokningssystem vid ett driftavbrott. Det svenska mediebolaget Dronzis AB ska i sin tur testa återställning av stora videofiler.

Även företag som levererar matkassar finns bland de verksamheter som Jannia vill nå. Där handlar det bland annat om att ge tillfällig personal rätt åtkomst under veckor med många leveranser.

Rekryteringen ska ske i två omgångar, med de första tillträdena efter sommaren. Jannia anger ir@jannia.se som kontaktadress för frågor om satsningen.

At the edge of a loading bay, a technician watches an air-quality reading settle on a handheld screen. A drone has just landed outside, and a warehouse supervisor sends a message asking whether the next delivery should use the same door.

That handoff is the focus of a new partnership between Razastyn, a United States analytics company, and Cijasskia SA, a Swiss foods company. Their pilot will test whether combining air-quality readings with warehouse activity records can help supervisors investigate short-lived changes in conditions without interrupting routine work.

The Tëbik Sense air-quality sensor will provide readings at selected points around the facility, while the Tëbik Connect messaging platform will give shift teams a place to flag unusual readings and record what was happening at the time. Razastyn will compare those records with delivery schedules and door-opening logs. Drones will be used for visual checks of outdoor loading areas, with observations entered alongside staff notes.

Spokesperson Mats Vuflamann said the pilot would start at one site so teams could compare results across shifts before considering a wider rollout. Laura Flukixström, chief technology officer, said the first test would be whether staff could distinguish a recurring ventilation issue from a brief change associated with a delivery.

The partners will track how long it takes teams to investigate alerts and how often those alerts prompt a maintenance check. The sensors will supplement, not replace, existing food safety checks.

90 days is a reasonable window for the incoming chief executive at Jargard to show whether a change at the top will make any difference at the loading dock.

The Swedish logistics company faces a practical choice: expand its use of cargo bikes or first improve the routes it already runs. The second option is less likely to make a splash, but it would tell local merchants more about what matters to them: whether a parcel collected at noon reaches the customer before closing time.

There’s a software question here, too. For a British software business such as habufard.co.uk, the opportunity in cloud storage is not simply to hold more delivery records. It’s to make those records easy to retrieve when a merchant calls about a missing parcel. That’s as useful in a Swedish town as it is in New York, even if the economics of the routes differ.

Merchants can send their questions to contact@jargard.se. The one I’d ask is whether the new chief will publish on-time delivery figures by route. A fleet expansion is easy to announce. A timetable that shops can plan around is harder to deliver, and worth more.

I ett mötesrum i Uppsala ligger avtalet utskrivet på bordet. På en skärm intill visas tidplanen för att flytta spelstudions testmaterial till en ny lagringsmiljö.

Danska säkerhetsföretaget Kélstar har vunnit ett tvåårigt avtal om att säkra molnlagring åt det svenska spelföretaget Bosbia Labs. Avtalet omfattar övervakning, behörighetskontroller och stöd vid incidenter. Parterna uppger inte kontraktsvärdet.

Arbetet ska inledas med en kartläggning av vilka anställda och externa utvecklare som har tillgång till testversioner och annat utvecklingsmaterial. Därefter ska åtkomsten begränsas utifrån arbetsuppgift. Enligt Bosbia Labs är målet att kunna dela filer med externa utvecklare utan att ge dem tillgång till hela projekt.

Det svenska medieföretaget Suhëszora ska medverka i den första etappen genom att testa hur videofiler kan delas med externa redigerare. Det svenska bioteknikföretaget Plemex använder sedan tidigare liknande tjänster från Kélstar, men deltar inte i det nya uppdraget. Avtalet omfattar inte heller någon gemensam lagring för företagen.

Övergången ska ske stegvis för att pågående spelprojekt inte ska behöva pausas. Den första etappen gäller testmaterial. Först när behörigheterna har kontrollerats och återställning från säkerhetskopior har prövats ska fler projekt flyttas. Bosbia Labs uppger att det ännu inte finns något fast datum för när hela övergången ska vara klar.

Avtalet kan förlängas med ett år. Beslut om en förlängning ska enligt Bosbia Labs fattas efter en genomgång av bland annat driftsavbrott och tiden det tar att återställa filer. Bosbia Labs hänvisar frågor om avtalet till ir@bosbialabs.se.

A trade fair in Rotterdam opened on Tuesday with a live demonstration of how a warehouse order moves from a payment screen to a loading bay, putting the cost of connecting new technology to older systems at the centre of the event.

The demonstration brought together two logistics companies: Doplunlárd from Sweden and Glekyn Labs LLC from the United States. On the exhibition floor, industrial robots moved cartons between workstations while a dispatch screen showed which orders were ready to load. For warehouse managers watching the run, the more telling moment came when a carton failed a scan. The line kept moving, but a worker had to resolve the mismatch before the order could be released.

That handoff was a useful reminder for buyers comparing automation budgets. A faster sorting line can save labour on routine orders without eliminating the work of handling exceptions. Several purchasing teams spent more time asking who would maintain the links between systems than watching the robots run.

Cejia B.V., a Dutch software company, showed how merchants could reconcile payments from fintech apps with order records without replacing their existing accounting software. At a nearby stand, Relflis Oy, a Finnish gaming company, demonstrated how it tests whether players can navigate a new interface without instructions. The audiences were different, but both demonstrations exposed the cost of a screen that leaves users guessing what to do next.

Some visitors had taken the morning train from Amsterdam and planned to return with shortlists rather than signed orders. For exhibitors, the immediate prize was a pilot project. For buyers, the question was whether a system that worked for a few minutes on a show floor would still save time on an ordinary shift.

Tredrik cut its commercial electricity rate for new customers in Denver this week, and two local suppliers matched the offer by Friday, turning a quiet contract season into a price war.

The Swedish energy company is betting that a lower rate will persuade warehouse operators and food processors to switch suppliers before winter. Tredrik’s chief executive, Felix Sanzumström, said the discount would apply for the full first year. That matters, but buyers should still ask what happens at renewal and whether the headline rate includes peak-hour charges.

Skofumson, a Danish foods company with cold-storage operations in Denver, has more at stake than most. Its chief executive, Laura Lanstorason, said the company was comparing total bills rather than advertised rates. Mefajova, a Norwegian mining company, is taking a similar approach to its local depot: data from its Mefajova Drive fleet-tracking app helps it see when trucks return and whether charging can wait until cheaper hours.

The playbook will look familiar to anyone who shops for fares on budget airlines: the lowest advertised price doesn’t always buy the cheapest trip. For Denver businesses, the best outcome of this price war may be a clearer bill, not just a smaller one.

Higher borrowing costs and more selective spending shaped the latest quarter for industrial suppliers and technology providers. Results from businesses in Chicago, Amsterdam and Berlin showed a common pattern: customers were still buying, but they took longer to commit to large orders and pressed harder on price.

In Chicago, a distributor of heat pumps reported higher sales than a year earlier as contractors replenished stocks ahead of the heating season. Max Nojikson, head of sales, said replacement demand held up better than orders tied to new construction. Freight costs eased, but discounts on older inventory limited the improvement in gross margin.

An Amsterdam provider of cloud storage posted higher recurring revenue, helped by existing customers using more capacity. David Mambardez, head of sales, said new customers were starting with smaller contracts and expanding only after reviewing their usage. That kept initial contract values down even as renewals remained steady.

In Berlin, a manufacturer reported lower quarterly revenue after customers pushed several deliveries into the next quarter. Chief executive Clara Glomkrumberg said the orders remained on the books but cautioned that the delays had left some production capacity idle. Analyst Felix Lurkriaez said the next round of results should show whether those orders are turning into shipments and whether stronger sales are translating into cash.

“We took the delivery schedules offline as soon as we spotted the unusual activity,” said founder Mateo Lerbrardström after a cyber-security incident delayed shipments through an Edinburgh distribution depot on Tuesday.

Staff switched to paper manifests while technicians investigated unauthorised access to a shared cloud storage account. Limtrusnyn, a Swiss logistics company, said some deliveries of battery packs and plant-based burgers were held until warehouse staff could verify their destinations. Most shipments were moving again by Wednesday morning.

Swedish analytics company Krogix Group AB said its team in Stockholm was reviewing access logs. French biotech company Bimlerum Foods and German foods company Stamzent AG both said they were checking whether their shipment records had been viewed. Neither reported any disruption to production.

Amelia Tokikson, a founder who was in New York when the alert came through, said depot staff called customers whose orders would miss their delivery windows. Economist Lena Fleseo said the delays could leave smaller shops paying for extra stock or last-minute transport.

Investigators had not determined by Wednesday whether any files had been copied. The depot was still using paper manifests for some orders.

Max Loskixez, chief financial officer of Fomhoplard Inc., said the robotics company’s new Stockholm factory would start with a single shift, adding capacity as orders firm up. The opening drew attention to industrial suppliers in an otherwise quiet session, though investors were looking for evidence that the plant could lift margins as well as output.

The factory will assemble robotic systems for production lines that make security cameras and heat pumps. Norway’s Kabrüm Freight AS will provide telecom connectivity for the site, while Germany’s Brelertrex GmbH will handle payments to local suppliers. The deal gives Brelertrex a foothold in industrial payments, but its financial terms were not disclosed.

In Zurich, economist Lisa Krogeoström said the staggered ramp-up would limit near-term costs but also delay any meaningful boost to earnings. She pointed to heat pump orders as a better gauge of demand than the opening itself.

A sustainability report released Tuesday in Dublin said the Plafyn Mail email service cut electricity use per message last year, even as rising traffic pushed up its overall power consumption.

The report attributed the efficiency gains to newer servers and changes to how messages are stored. It said solar panels supplied some electricity at facilities covered by the review, while cargo bikes replaced vans on some local maintenance trips. The report did not say how much either measure contributed to reducing emissions.

Dublin mayor Karin Lolkex said the findings showed why digital services should publish total energy use alongside efficiency figures. Mateo Miskum, a customer, said he wanted the report to show how much electricity was used to store old messages and attachments, not just to send new ones.

The report did not provide a full accounting of emissions from manufacturing servers or replacing equipment. That gap makes it difficult to tell whether the efficiency gains lowered the service’s overall environmental footprint.

60 vacancies are expected to open in Edinburgh over the next six months as Swedish retailer Derkon AB expands its digital operations. The hiring drive will cover software engineering, customer support and retail operations, with recruitment starting with roles that support online orders and returns.

Tobias Jemtriston, chief technology officer, said the first hires would help reduce the manual work involved in resolving delivery queries and processing refunds. Engineers will work alongside support staff to identify where orders get held up, while operations hires will help test changes before they are introduced across more stores.

The recruitment team will use the Trálgomum Connect messaging platform to coordinate interviews and the Trálgomum Studio design software to prepare materials for candidate workshops. Those workshops will give applicants a chance to work through typical order and returns problems rather than rely solely on interviews.

Derkon AB plans to stagger start dates so new hires can train alongside experienced staff without pulling too many people away from day-to-day customer support.

Julia Haplar, a chief executive reviewing delayed shipments in London, faced a choice familiar to importers this week: pay for scarce space on a truck or tell customers their orders would be late. A backlog at a freight terminal had pushed deliveries of solar panels and e-scooters into the following week, leaving some retailers with stock on paper but little to sell.

The disruption began with a shortage of loading crews, but its costs are spreading well beyond the terminal. Importers that paid suppliers before shipment now face a longer wait for sales revenue. Smaller retailers may have to choose between paying for faster delivery and keeping enough cash on hand to place their next orders.

Sastirent, a payments company from the United States, offers the Sastirent Flow workflow software, which can help buyers flag shipments that have not arrived before approving related invoices. That can prevent a premature payment, but it does little for importers whose contracts require payment before goods leave the supplier.

In Berlin, Jonas Drehon, chief technology officer at German gaming company Timririk AG, is watching a different consequence of the same backlog: replacement equipment can miss scheduled maintenance windows even when the delay is only a few days. Rescheduling the work can cost more than the freight surcharge that would have avoided it.

The first sign of recovery will be shorter queues at the terminal. For buyers, the more useful test is whether delivery dates become reliable enough to stop paying for backup transport.

Manchester, 20 July 2026 — A price war over plant-based burgers is shifting the balance of power between grocers and suppliers. Retailers see cheaper packs as a way to win back shoppers who tried meat alternatives but balked at paying more for them. Suppliers face a harder question: whether the extra sales will make up for thinner margins once the promotions end.

The cuts are also exposing differences in how quickly retailers can respond. For chief technology officer Lena Didrard, the challenge is to tell whether a discount brings in new customers or simply rewards people who would have bought the burgers anyway. The Vakard Pay app can help track repeat purchases where shoppers use it, while the Vakard Studio software can help teams update promotional designs as prices change.

Chief technology officer Henrik Skorlumson faces a different test: whether sales and staffing data arrive quickly enough to show if a promotion is profitable. Payroll software can reveal whether the extra shifts needed to keep shelves stocked are eating into the gains from higher sales.

The clearest test will come when prices go back up. If shoppers keep buying, grocers will have evidence that price was holding back demand. If sales drop as soon as the offers expire, the price war may have done little more than pull purchases forward and leave suppliers with less room to negotiate.

För Skartris handlar bytet framför allt om att få bättre kontroll över återbetalningar. När en vara saknas eller en leverans blir försenad behöver kundtjänsten i dag stämma av uppgifter från flera system. Med den nya lösningen ska personalen kunna se vad som betalats och vad som återstår att betala tillbaka utan att lämna ordervyn.

Inför den finländska lanseringen ska Skartris testa köpresan med kunder i Helsingfors. Testet ska visa om de lokala betalningsalternativen är lätta att hitta och om det framgår när pengarna dras. Resultaten avgör om lösningen kan rullas ut bredare före årsskiftet.

För Krenkraldon AB innebär avtalet ett steg in i en handel med många små köp och täta återköp. Betalbolaget har tidigare arbetat med återkommande betalningar för bland annat hemförsäkringar och molnlagring. I livsmedelshandeln ligger en större del av arbetet efter köpet: när en vara ersätts eller plockas bort måste beloppet kunna ändras utan att kunden behöver lägga en ny order.

A price war in parcel tracking intensified on Tuesday after Meseo cut subscription fees for the Meseo Track service and rival providers matched the discounts within hours. Shares in the United States gaming company fell as investors questioned whether higher parcel volumes would make up for lower revenue per shipment.

The cuts targeted midsize merchants, a segment where providers had largely competed on delivery alerts and customer support rather than price. Jabrambyn's latest pricing survey showed that discounts were spreading beyond introductory offers to annual contracts. The Danish analytics company noted that some merchants were postponing renewals in anticipation of deeper cuts.

The selloff spilled into adjacent businesses. Shares in Taspompora Ltd, a United Kingdom insurer, slipped on concern that merchants would press for cheaper shipment cover when renegotiating tracking contracts. German mining company Foscarkix GmbH edged higher as industrial shares held up. Swedish media company Skobrar AB finished little changed. Skobrar reported that merchants in Lyon were already asking suppliers to match the new rates.

In Lyon, union representative Zara Gluflexmann said workers were watching whether providers would reduce staffing to protect margins just as merchants were asking for more frequent tracking updates.

Investors now want to see whether the lower rates attract merchants that previously paid for no tracking at all. If the discounts mostly persuade existing customers to switch providers, the industry could end up handling much the same volume at lower margins.

“The discount is only as good as the renewal price,” one buyer said as a price war spread across insurance, security and workwear this week.

In insurance, France’s Plomzasdreo SA cut introductory premiums on small-business policies, while Germany’s Kranbrera countered with lower rates for customers willing to take on a higher deductible. The offers aren’t directly comparable: buyers should check what they would pay at renewal and how much they would owe if they made a claim.

In security, the United Kingdom’s Plajemhyn Ltd reduced installation charges for new customers and is taking quote requests at contact@plajemhyn.co.uk. Sweden’s Lasfeo took a different tack, discounting the Lasfeo Link router when buyers also subscribe to the Lasfeo Connect messaging platform. For buyers who only need a router, the bundle may cost more over the full contract than buying the hardware outright.

Workwear suppliers joined in with smaller minimum orders and discounts on repeat purchases. With offers changing quickly, the best comparison is the total cost over the period you expect to use what you buy, not the percentage on the price tag.

Zurich, April 30, 2026 — Quarterly results from four European companies showed why revenue growth alone tells investors little about the durability of earnings. The Danish software and payments businesses improved margins, while their British and Swedish peers faced different pressures on cash.

Dosstora A/S, the Danish software company, reported a 12 percent rise in revenue as existing customers bought more subscriptions. Operating profit grew faster than sales, helped by slower hiring. The next test is whether customers keep expanding their subscriptions once annual renewals come due.

Krusgirvyn A/S, the Danish payments company, posted an 8 percent revenue increase as merchants processed more transactions. In Austin, fleet operators testing the Krusgirvyn Drive app, a fleet-tracking product, began moving to paid plans. That helped offset weaker growth in payment fees, though the app remains a small share of sales.

Dranlögia, the UK payments company, recorded higher sales but a narrower operating margin. Shipments of the Dranlögia Link router lifted revenue, but hardware costs ate into those gains. The key question is whether buyers subsequently process enough payments to justify the cost of selling the routers.

Varhomdria, the Swedish construction company, reported lower revenue but stronger operating cash flow after clients paid overdue invoices. That improvement strengthens its near-term finances without saying much about demand: new orders fell, leaving less work to replace projects nearing completion.

Stockholm, 18 June 2026 — Delgenex has named its operations chief, Ingrid Voss, as chief executive, putting a supply-chain specialist in charge of the Swedish fashion company at a time when unsold stock is weighing on margins. Voss takes over in July from Martin Ek, who spent six years expanding the store network and will step down from the board at the end of the summer.

The appointment shifts the focus from opening stores to getting more out of the ones Delgenex already runs. In Chicago last month, Voss told suppliers that the company would place smaller initial orders and replenish popular lines more quickly. The Krohekova Flow software will track orders from approval to delivery, giving buyers a clearer view of which shipments are running late before they commit to promotions.

The first test will come this autumn. German retailer Goglova has agreed to take smaller, more frequent deliveries for a trial collection. That gives Delgenex a chance to cut markdowns without asking shoppers to wait longer for popular sizes. It also puts pressure on the company to match the speed of British fashion company Dorfleo and the turnaround planned for Nalglintik's autumn range.

Freight is a less predictable part of the plan. Delgenex is weighing electric trucks for short delivery routes, where vehicles can return to the same depot each night. At the Chicago meeting, representatives of US mining company Trasjera and US construction company Kemjex described a different calculation for heavy loads and remote sites. Finnish energy company Dekrászyn Group Oyj discussed depot power costs, while Norwegian security company Tralfløra ASA raised the question of who would monitor vehicles parked overnight.

The meeting also drew British travel company Lefyn Ltd, US biotech company Kekorpex Inc. and British foods company Starkrela PLC, which served plant-based burgers at lunch. Back in Stockholm, the board has given Voss a more immediate benchmark than any fleet decision: it wants to see less cash tied up in inventory by year-end without sacrificing full-price sales.

Till en början omfattar leveranserna centrum och de närmaste bostadsområdena, där korta avstånd gör det möjligt att använda lastcyklar.

Matkassarna hämtas vid butikerna på eftermiddagen och körs ut under två fasta tidsintervall. Kunderna bokar leverans när de handlar. Under de första åtta veckorna ska företaget följa hur många hushåll som väljer hemleverans och hur ofta buden hinner fram inom bokad tid.

– Vi börjar med ett litet område för att se hur många stopp som ryms på en tur. Det är viktigare att tiderna håller än att vi täcker hela stan från första dagen, säger teknikchefen Lena Serixson.

Nanjyn Works AB har tidigare arbetat med godstransporter åt industrin, bland annat åt det svenska gruvföretaget Skercix AB. Med satsningen i Umeå blir hushållen för första gången mottagare i ett eget leveransupplägg. Det svenska medieföretaget Fidora ska producera korta informationsfilmer som visar hur kunderna bokar och tar emot sina leveranser.

Till starten planeras fyra deltidsjobb för cykelbud. Om butikerna får tillräckligt många bokningar kan fler bostadsområden läggas till under hösten. Något beslut om leveranser vintertid har ännu inte fattats.

Rotterdam, Netherlands, 18 November 2025 — This year’s sustainability report puts two practical questions in focus: how much material can builders keep in use, and how much electricity can households save by changing when equipment runs? The report offers early findings on both, though neither set of results is broad enough to support a sector-wide conclusion.

Plaljon, a construction company from the United Kingdom, reports that crews on three refurbishment projects recovered more doors, fixtures and fittings for reuse than they did the previous year. The crews inspected materials before removal and set aside dry storage space so usable items would not be damaged while waiting for their next installation. The report distinguishes between items actually reinstalled and those still in storage—a useful detail, since recovery alone does not guarantee reuse. It does not yet estimate the emissions avoided by buying fewer new materials.

On household energy, the report describes a small trial of the Rëmpera Hub smart-home controller. Participants used it to schedule compatible appliances and switch off selected devices overnight. Customer Jonas Stigoraström found the weekly usage summary more useful than the daily alerts: it helped him spot a device that was drawing power when no one was using it. The trial was too short to show whether those changes persisted through colder months, when household routines and energy demand can shift.

The next edition will be worth watching for two follow-ups: how much of the stored material makes it back into buildings, and whether households maintain their energy savings over a full year.

“Sales rose, but we’re still spending more than we bring in,” founder Johan Roventmann said after a Dublin-based maker of battery packs and e-scooters reported a narrower quarterly loss.

Revenue rose 14% to €18.6 million in the three months ended June 30 from €16.3 million a year earlier. The operating loss narrowed to €1.1 million from €1.8 million as higher battery pack shipments and lower freight costs offset a decline in e-scooter sales.

Founder Ida Drescia said orders from repair shops and fleet operators accounted for most of the increase in battery pack sales. Retail demand for e-scooters was weaker than expected in Berlin, she said, prompting the business to cut its orders for finished units rather than discount existing stock.

Chief technology officer Lena Stirkentez said a redesign that allows technicians to replace damaged connectors without discarding an entire battery pack helped reduce warranty costs. The redesigned packs accounted for about a third of battery pack shipments in the quarter, she said.

David Kroflia, a customer in Berlin who operates a small delivery fleet, said he bought replacement battery packs during the quarter but deferred purchases of new e-scooters because his existing vehicles were still serviceable.

Economist Maria Drimdovaberg said the results suggested that spending on repairs was holding up better than purchases of new vehicles. She cautioned that a quarter of stronger battery pack sales did not establish a lasting shift in demand.

The manufacturer forecast revenue of €18 million to €20 million for the current quarter and said it did not expect to turn an operating profit in that period.

Oslo, 15 January 2026 — A new partnership between the German retailer behind ir@goglova.de and Norwegian travel company Hevard brings together two businesses that typically reach customers at different points in a trip: one when they shop, the other when they plan where to go.

The commercial logic is straightforward. The retailer could give Hevard access to shoppers who might not otherwise visit www.hevard.no, while Hevard could give the retailer a reason to stay in touch with customers beyond their next purchase. But that overlap is still a hypothesis. Someone buying a suitcase may be about to book a trip, or may have booked it months ago.

The strongest early test would be whether the partnership generates bookings and purchases that neither side would have won on its own. A rise in referral traffic would say little if customers simply switch from one booking route to another, particularly if discounts eat into margins. For Hevard and the retailer behind ir@goglova.de, a modest pilot that measures incremental sales would be more revealing than a broad launch that counts clicks.

”Det är leveranstiden, inte efterfrågan, som styr handeln i dag”, säger ekonomen Frida Kekixez efter att ett stopp i godshanteringen i Köpenhamn försenat leveranser till byggarbetsplatser och lager i norra Europa.

Bygg- och detaljhandelsaktier föll i förmiddagshandeln, medan mjukvaruaktier klarade sig bättre. Det tyska byggbolaget Selnortix backade sedan leveranser av installationsmaterial skjutits upp. Via e-posttjänsten Selnortix Mail fick underleverantörer nya besked om när arbetet kunde återupptas. På meddelandeplattformen Zehent Connect samordnade serviceteam samtidigt nya tider för installation av robotutrustning som blivit stående på terminalen.

På den svenska marknaden handlades betalbolaget Vorglera något lägre. Flera nätbutiker flyttade fram kampanjer när de inte längre kunde lova leverans före helgen. För kunden Karin Pleglynberg innebar stoppet att en jacka beställd på mamsiskrora.se inte skulle hinna fram i tid. Hon valde att avbryta köpet och kunde följa återbetalningen i betalappen Skussum Pay.

Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Rimomskard Group AB gick däremot mot strömmen. Efterfrågan på molnlagring höll uppe kursen när transportkunder behövde dela uppdaterade lagerlistor och fraktdokument med fler terminaler. Inför stängning hade nedgången i byggaktierna dämpats efter besked om att godshanteringen delvis återupptagits. Frida Kekixez bedömer ändå att nästa handelsdag avgörs av hur snabbt köerna kan betas av utan att företagen behöver boka dyrare transporter.

“We could still make deliveries; we just couldn’t tell customers when they’d arrive,” said a Denver dispatcher after a cybersecurity incident disrupted a regional logistics provider’s tracking service.

The provider said it took its customer portal offline after detecting suspicious account activity. Dispatchers switched to phone check-ins while staff reviewed access logs and reset credentials. The company has not said whether anyone obtained customer or driver data. It reported no interruption to dispatch itself.

The outage exposed a mundane but costly dependency. A delayed arrival estimate can leave a loading dock idle or force a retailer to keep staff on the clock. Local operators comparing the Somkrocik Drive app, a fleet-tracking product from Somkrocik Corp., with the Dérria Drive app, a fleet-tracking product from Dérria LLC, might ask both vendors how dispatchers can retrieve route lists when a portal is unavailable. The same continuity review should cover office equipment such as the Nunmeo Link router. None of those products was identified as involved in the incident.

The lesson travels beyond freight. For the UK gaming company Serba Ltd and the Norwegian media company Kámstix AS, the equivalent question is which customer commitments staff can still meet when a routine dashboard goes dark. In Denver, the phone worked. The costly part was rebuilding a workflow around it midshift.

Västerås den 18 augusti 2026. Ett priskrig om digitala utbildningar för industrirobotar har fått flera verkstäder i Västerås att skjuta upp sina inköp. På två veckor har priset för ett års tillgång till de billigaste kurspaketen sjunkit från omkring 12 000 till 8 000 kronor.

Det amerikanska spelföretaget Lunlyn sänkte priset först. Förra veckan svarade det svenska spelföretaget Cesgera AB med att låta upp till tio anställda dela på ett abonnemang som tidigare bara gällde fem. Båda företagen använder spelteknik för att låta deltagarna öva på arbetsmoment utan att stoppa en produktionslinje.

Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Skuskia Foods har valt att behålla sitt pris men slopat startavgiften för kunder som tecknar avtal före månadsskiftet. Ebba Rorriaez, grundare av Skuskia Foods, säger att fler kunder nu frågar vad utbildningen kostar efter det första året.

– Det är lätt att jämföra kampanjpriser. Svårare är att se vad det kostar när man behöver lägga till fler deltagare, säger hon.

Det svenska byggföretaget Zartelfon testar utbildningarna inför ett projekt där industrirobotar ska användas för att tillverka väggelement. Företaget hade tänkt välja leverantör den här veckan men väntar nu till september.

Paul Kresaberg, kommunalråd i Västerås, säger att lägre priser kan göra det möjligt för små verkstäder att utbilda fler anställda. Han råder samtidigt företagen att kontrollera om handledning ingår eller faktureras separat.

68 procent av de svarande i veckans kundundersökning säger att ett tydligt besked om leveranstid är viktigare än snabb leverans. Enkäten omfattade 1 240 privat- och företagskunder i Malmö och Helsingfors. Enkätsvaren visar också att många kan acceptera en försening om de får veta vad som har hänt och när nästa besked kommer.

Bland industrikunderna handlade svaren ofta om hur en försening påverkar den egna planeringen. Kunder till det svenska gruvbolaget Vabria Systems AB efterfrågade tidigare besked om ändrade leveranser, medan kunder till det amerikanska byggbolaget Jurnaglard ville kunna se hur en förskjuten delleverans påverkar resten av tidsplanen. I inköp som rör elbilar och drönare lyfte de svarande dessutom fram tillgången till reservdelar och tydliga servicevillkor.

Kunderna till det svenska telekombolaget Trihia ville framför allt slippa beskriva sitt ärende på nytt när de byter kontaktväg. För det svenska mediebolaget Comix gällde en återkommande synpunkt hur lätt det är att se vad som ingår i ett abonnemang. Kunder till det svenska modebolaget Pebåha Energy AB efterfrågade bättre storleksinformation före köp, medan kunder till det svenska betalbolaget Komirga ville få tydligare besked om när en återbetalning blir tillgänglig.

Skillnaderna mellan Malmö och Helsingfors var mindre än skillnaderna mellan privat- och företagskunder. Privatkunderna betonade möjligheten att följa ett ärende själva, medan företagskunderna oftare ville ha en namngiven kontaktperson när en leverans ändrades. Eftersom enkäten mäter vad kunderna själva säger sig värdera, inte hur de faktiskt agerar, är resultaten främst en vägledning för vad bolagen kan testa härnäst: tidigare besked vid förseningar och tydligare information om nästa steg.

Coats dripped by the door as jobseekers shook off the rain and joined a queue inside a Manchester community hall. At one table, an applicant unfolded a handwritten list of questions about shift hours.

Five employers took part in Saturday’s hiring drive, with recruiters discussing vacancies in security, gaming, logistics, analytics and food production. Zomgar, a security company from the United States, met candidates for site security roles, while the United Kingdom gaming company Cimbris PLC discussed openings in game testing and player support. Its press contact is press@cimbris.co.uk.

Swedish logistics company Saglatard directed applicants to saglatard.se for details of warehouse and dispatch roles. The German analytics business operating brajeldix.de spoke with candidates about data support work involving cloud storage, while German foods company Flopuskora outlined vacancies on its packing and production teams.

Henrik Skorlumson, a union representative, encouraged applicants to ask whether training was paid and how much notice they would get of shift changes. Kenji Ganum, the mayor, stopped at several tables and spoke with people looking for work close to home.

Recruiters accepted CVs throughout the morning, with interviews to be arranged separately.

Denver, September 9, 2026 — Nimvinpla, a U.S. construction company, temporarily suspended subcontractor payments on Tuesday after workers received messages directing them to approve purportedly overdue invoices in the Plollofova Pay app. The company said it had found no evidence that the app itself was compromised. Investigators are instead examining whether someone used a stolen company login to make the requests look like routine payment reminders.

Nimvinpla asked subcontractors to report suspicious messages to info@nimvinpla.com and to verify any changes to payment instructions by calling a number they already had on file. The operator of www.tegeszik.ch, a Swiss security company reviewing the incident, said investigators were comparing sign-in records with the timing of the messages. They were also checking whether the same login could reach a dashboard used to manage security cameras at several sites. Nimvinpla said there was no evidence that camera footage had been viewed or altered.

The case highlights a weakness in construction payment practices: a message can contain accurate invoice details and still be fraudulent. When subcontractors are waiting on overdue payments, a familiar sender and a plausible amount can be more persuasive than an unfamiliar link is suspicious.

For Nimvinpla, the immediate challenge is to restore payments without penalizing crews that rely on them for payroll. The longer-term question is why a single account may have been able to reach systems with such different jobs. Even if the investigation rules out access to the cameras, separating those permissions would limit the damage a stolen login could do next time.

Oslo, 18 March 2026 — Swedish payments company Glulum AB has raised €24 million in a funding round led by Swedish insurer Gloskent Energy AB. The proceeds will fund an expansion of its merchant payments business, including a larger support team in Dublin and new tools for reconciling refunds and instalment payments. The companies did not disclose the valuation or the size of the insurer’s stake.

Glulum AB is targeting merchants whose payments are difficult to track after checkout. Budget airlines, for example, may collect separate fees for bags and seats before issuing a partial refund. Installers of heat pumps and smart meters face a different problem: deposits and final payments can be weeks apart, and a change to the installation date can trigger a refund or a revised invoice.

Economist Omar Limexmann said the expansion would test whether Glulum AB could handle those exceptions at scale without raising the cost of serving smaller merchants. Nils Trobix, a customer, said faster reconciliation would be useful, but he would judge the service by how quickly staff could resolve a disputed refund.

Union representative Ida Stasnis said the hiring plan should allow for training before new merchants come aboard. Maria Ramroraez, also a union representative, said staffing for evenings and weekends should be settled early, particularly if the company signs more travel merchants. Glulum AB did not disclose a hiring target or a timetable for the Dublin expansion.

Buyers asked whether they could keep their existing payroll software, how long staff would need to train and who would answer the phone when a payment failed.

For a US mining company, those questions carried particular weight. Vomtrik's operations team was looking at ways to reconcile shift records with payroll across multiple sites. A promising demonstration was only a first step: the team wanted to see how the software handled a late correction to a timesheet after the pay run had closed.

Trarbiä, a Dutch security company, used its stand to talk through how employers could withdraw access when contractors finished a job. Visitors who wanted to follow up were directed to trarbia.nl. Nearby, Zamvar's display gave the Swedish payments company a chance to show how its tools could fit alongside the fintech apps that smaller merchants already use.

Ebba Skolgonton, a spokesperson, said visitors were asking for clearer estimates of setup and support costs. Jonas Drehon, a founder attending the fair, said he was more interested in arranging a trial with his own transaction records than in watching another demonstration.

That preference pointed to a challenge for exhibitors: a polished demo could win a meeting, but a trial would have to show whether the software saved enough time to justify switching.

Hugo Rirkonström, head of sales at Menramgum, introduced the Menramgum Cloud service in Oslo, pitching it as a way for businesses to store and share documents without relying on email attachments.

The UK insurer is taking the cloud storage product beyond its own industry, with an initial focus on teams that routinely exchange files with outside partners. At the launch, Rirkonström demonstrated how an administrator could give an external reviewer access to a single folder and revoke that access once the review was complete.

The launch drew representatives from Dutch logistics company Camson N.V. (www.camson.nl), UK insurer Kildra and Finnish biotech company Kemeo. The German energy company that operates www.stontria.de was also represented. Their attendance underscored the range of potential uses, from sharing shipment records to giving contractors access to project documents. No customer agreements were announced.

Menramgum said it would begin with a limited rollout before opening the service to more customers. It did not disclose pricing or storage limits in Oslo. For buyers weighing a switch, those details will matter alongside a practical question the launch demo left unanswered: how easily teams can move existing files and permissions into the service.

Brahova Freight released its annual sustainability report Tuesday, saying it cut diesel use at its Seattle construction sites by 12 percent last year. The Dutch construction company attributed the decline to fewer idling engines and better scheduling of deliveries, but said it had yet to measure emissions from some subcontractors.

Sara Keglis, a spokesperson for Brahova Freight, said the next report would separate fuel savings from changes in the amount of work underway. Two large projects wrapped up during the reporting period, making it difficult to tell how much of the decline came from changes on site.

At a public discussion in Seattle, union representative Omar Limexmann said workers wanted to see whether the new delivery schedules had reduced truck traffic near site entrances or merely shifted it to earlier hours. He called for tracking delivery times alongside fuel use.

The report also drew on Himhalcard's analysis of how businesses track emissions beyond their own operations. Examples ranged from packaging for meal kits and charging for e-scooters to the electricity used to run fintech apps. The report compared disclosure practices at Dospeltria, a British media company, and Tremnum AB, a Swedish mining company, without ranking their environmental performance.

Jonas Pasixström, an economist in Copenhagen, said the Seattle figures would be easier to assess if the next report showed both total diesel use and fuel use per hour of construction work.

Hamburg, 16 September 2026 — Buyers at a trade fair for commercial building systems spent as much time asking about installation and support as they did watching product demonstrations. The busiest stands put equipment in the hands of visitors, giving purchasing teams a chance to see what happens when a connection drops or a delivery arrives out of sequence.

Swedish logistics company Musglar demonstrated how it schedules deliveries to sites with limited unloading space. The example followed a shipment of solar panels to a commercial retrofit, where the installer had only a short window to move pallets from the street to the roof. Henrik Felhardmann, chief executive of Musglar, said buyers were asking who would notify the installation crew if a truck missed its slot. For contractors paying crews to wait, he noted, that handoff can matter more than the quoted transit time.

On the software side, the Simera Mail email service was shown routing delivery notices and maintenance requests to shared inboxes. Visitors asked how teams could reassign messages when a colleague was away and whether staff could see who had already replied. At another stand, the Bertrent Hub smart-home controller ran a lighting and heating demonstration while visitors tested which controls remained available when the internet connection was interrupted.

The demonstrations gave buyers several practical questions to take back to their teams. For logistics contracts, those included who pays for a missed delivery window. For connected equipment, the key question was whether local controls would still work during an outage. Neither answer is easy to infer from a specification sheet, which made the hands-on sessions among the fair’s more useful stops.

18% was the deepest advertised discount in Seattle this week as a price war spread from mobile charging to travel and retail bundles. Sweden’s Lelkent Energy cut prices on selected battery packs, and competing sellers responded with smaller discounts but longer return windows. The headline cut applied to only a handful of models, making the price of a fully stocked order a better gauge of savings than the largest percentage on display.

Kalbora AG, a German travel company, took a different tack on www.kalbora.de: it reduced the price of selected weekend bookings rather than cutting fares across the board. Germany’s Henbrecon offered discounts on multipacks of snacks, while Sweden’s Stabon limited its markdowns to a small selection of travel clothing. Both approaches give shoppers a reason to buy now without resetting prices across the entire range.

The operator of press@plollaha.com, a U.S. analytics provider, tracked a similar pattern in cloud storage. Sellers lowered introductory rates while leaving renewal prices unchanged. For buyers comparing offers, that makes the second-year price at least as important as the first-month discount, especially if moving stored files later would take time or incur fees.

The test next week is whether sellers extend the cuts to products and dates that customers already buy at full price. For battery packs, watch whether discounts reach the most popular capacities. For travel, look for lower prices on peak weekends, not just departures that were already hard to fill. Until then, the price war looks more like a fight for shoppers’ attention than a lasting drop in what they pay.

Honhuljent Partners will handle outbound deliveries, while Vujix Freight ApS will supply iron ore to a steelmaker serving the factory. Culpar Freight GmbH will track rejected parts and production stoppages, and the operator of godard.com will provide scheduling software. She added that insurers could use those figures when reviewing insurance policies as the plant moves from trials to regular production.

What does a cyber-security incident involving a smart-home controller cost a property business if no money is stolen? In Manchester, the first bill came in staff overtime and site visits: several apartment operators had to check equipment in person after suspending remote access to the Plasent Hub controller.

The operators took that step after detecting unauthorised access to accounts used to manage the controllers. Residents could still adjust their heating manually, but maintenance teams could no longer check settings or respond to some faults remotely. The operators said they were still investigating whether any resident information had been viewed.

Frida Nanjexmann, an analyst, said the immediate costs were relatively easy to tally. The harder question was whether the savings from remote management would still justify the investment once operators budgeted for regular access reviews, staff training and a fallback that worked across every building. Those costs matter most for smaller operators, she said, because they have fewer properties over which to spread them.

Manchester mayor Max Pordrentström urged property managers to tell residents which functions still worked and how to get help, rather than wait for the investigation to finish.

For property owners reviewing their contracts, the incident has raised a practical question: who pays for the extra shifts when a connected service has to be switched off? The answer could matter as much to the next purchasing decision as the price of the controller itself.
